subject: Just another way to attack mail-in ballots

body:
These USPS postmark changes are just the latest step taken by MAGA's vote suppressors to limit mail-in ballots.
Why? Because in recent elections, the percentage of people voting by mail hasn't favored their extremist candidates, and voter participation has actually increased via the use of vote-by-mail and drop boxes. This all leads to candidates MAGA doesn't like winning elections.
Team, these changes are about who has power now and how badly they want to keep it. RUSH $35 or more right now to help inform voters of this change and defend the use of mail-in ballots across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=031626_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
HuffPost: Mail-In Voters Could Face A New Obstacle This Midterm Season [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=031626_3&amount=25]
Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts.
How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control.
We have to make sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- from vote-by-mail, to their bills, their taxes, legal replies to companies, everything. What Americans think is the mailing deadline may not be the deadline anymore and that's a huge deal that's being under-reported by the media.
Team, Every voter needs to know about this massive change. Will you pitch in $35 or whatever you can today and help us spread the word about the USPS changes so we can protect mail-in ballots? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=031626_3&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

We're worried about every mail-in voter getting their ballot in on time, but especially those most vulnerable to this change, like the elderly, rural Americans who live far from USPS regional facilities, our military service members, and young people who are voting by mail away from home. None of them deserve to be disenfranchised from our elections over DOGE's cost-cutting measures.
Whether you can fuel our work today or not, we appreciate your support and we hope you can spread the word about this USPS change to your friends, family, and colleagues. You never know how a quick mention of something like this news might truly impact someone else's life.
Thank you,
The Voter Action Project Team

name: America Fitzpatrick, LCV
subject: DEVELOPING: MAGA Republicans aim to gut Grand Staircase-Escalante, test new plan for selling off public lands.
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM1NjEyMTcS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQyMTA2Mjk4MAS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Peter — The same Republicans who wanted to sell off our public lands
are back at it — this time they’ve introduced legislation to gut protections for
Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument in southern Utah. This legislation, introduced by Senator Mike Lee and Representative Celeste
Maloy, is an unprecedented attempt to overturn a national monument’s management
plan. If it succeeds, this maneuver could become part of the MAGA playbook for
dismantling protections for even more of our treasured public lands across the
country. We can’t give up on our public lands, Peter. Are you with us? LCV is mobilizing a major campaign to keep public lands in public hands — and we
need your support to reach our $25,000 goal. Right now, every contribution TRIPLES in impact, so please don’t wait. Renew your membership now to power our work before our 3X match expires on March 31. Right now, every $15=$45 >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/RZbkcRj2~ Grand Staircase-Escalante spans nearly 1.9 million acresof canyons, ancient fossil beds, sacred cultural sites, and essential wildlife
habitat. It is home to bighorn sheep, mule deer, and endangered and protected
species like the California condor and Bald Eagle. Current protections for Grand Staircase-Escalante reflect years of scientific
research, public comment, and collaboration with Tribal coalitions and local
communities. If enacted, Senator Lee’s attack would strip these critical
protections away — and the consequences could extend far beyond Utah and this
specific national monument. We need to make sure this doesn’t become the blueprint for dismantling national
monuments across the country. Public lands belong to all of us, not to corporate polluters or politicians looking for shortcuts to undermine
the protections communities have worked so hard to build together. Peter, we’re halfway through the month and we’re tracking short of our
$25,000 goal. These resources are critical for helping LCV respond to threats to our public lands — especially in the

body:
| Friend, do you remember when I first ran for Congress in 2022?

I defied the odds by winning a statewide race against our former governor Sarah Palin not only once, but _twice._

My victory showed that when grassroots power works together, we can take on the biggest challenges.

But here’s the truth about Sarah Palin:

You may not expect it, but we actually agree on a few things. We both believe that our representatives should work to lower costs and create jobs.

That may not seem like such a novel idea, but as you read this, DC politicians are more focused on party loyalty and their own wallets than getting things done for working families.

That’s why I decided to jump in this race for U.S. Senate. I’m running to take on the rigged system that’s hurting us all, but I can’t do it without your support.

Just like in 2022, it’s going to take a huge grassroots team to stand up to the DC establishment and win this race.

We have our first big FEC deadline coming up, and with it our first public report of how much support my campaign has. That’s why we need lots and lots of donations before then to demonstrate that we have what it takes to win.

If everyone reading this chipped in $10, we’d have what we need to hit our fundraising goals and take on the self-serving DC system in no time.

Not everyone can, so I’m counting on those of you who understand how important your support is before this deadline to give today.

subject: Women for Abdul just launched, and WOW!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1001&akid=1856%2E251025%2ENFBpNk ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1002&akid=1856%2E251025%2ENFBpNk ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter,

On Saturday, more than 150 women gathered in Pontiac to launch Women for
Abdul — our new initiative organizing women across Michigan to help elect
Abdul to the U.S. Senate.

[ Abdul ]Abdul taking a selfie at the event with a crowd of supporters smiling
and holding 'Women for Abdul' signs in the background

They came from all over the state: working moms, students, organizers, and
community leaders ready to build something bigger together.

We’re living through a time of profound change. Women across Michigan know
we need leaders with the courage and moral clarity to stand up to the
powerful interests that have deepened inequality and made it harder for
families to live stable, healthy lives.

That’s why a group of motivated women volunteers came together to launch
Women for Abdul. They know and believe that Abdul is the only candidate in
this race who:

* You can trust to fight for families
* Knows how to make government actually deliver services and resources
families need
* Has shown that he can clean up unhealthy environments our communities
are forced to endure
* Consistently opposes sending U.S. military funds overseas
* Believes that healthcare is a fundamental human right
* Courageously calls for abolishing ICE

Abdul often talks about the future he wants for his two daughters — one
where their rights are protected, their work is valued, and their
healthcare decisions are their own.

That future won’t build itself. It’ll take all of us.

That’s why we’re asking: [ https://go.abdulforsenate.com/women-for-abdul?utm_source=em20260316-1854 ]Will you join Women for Abdul today?

[ https://go.abdulforsenate.com/women-for-abdul?utm_source=em20260316-1854 ]Sign Up ››

Thanks so much,

Team Abdul

P.S. Abdul is speaking directly to campaign volunteers on our next
Statewide Organizing Call this Wednesday at 7 PM. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/706?utm_source=em20260316-1854&t=1004&akid=1856%2E251025%2ENFBpNk ]Sign up here if you
can make it!

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Emails like this help us stay connected with grassroots supporters like you, so thank you for taking the time to read this message. To contribute via check, please address it to Abdul for U.S. Senate, PO Box 126, St. Clair Shores, MI 48080.

Receive Fewer Emails: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/?t=1005&akid=1856%2E251025%2ENFBpNk
Update Your Information: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/signup/update-your-information
Unsubscribe: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe?t=1006&akid=1856%2E251025%2ENFBpNk

Email us: info@abdulformichigan.com
Volunteer: https://go.abdulforsenate.com/join

name: Judicial Watch Tipsheet
subject: Judicial Watch Sues Justice Department for Records Linking Norm Eisen to FBI’s ‘Arctic Frost’ Probe
body:
Judicial Watch announced today that it filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit against the U.S. Department of Justice for all records linking Norm Eisen to the FBI’s Biden-era “Arctic Frost” probe, specifically involving the Criminal Division, the Office of Information Policy, Attorney General Merrick Garland, Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and Special Counsel Jack Smith’s team (Judicial Watch, Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice (No. 1:26-cv-00746)).

Peter, Florida has long been the testing ground for some of the GOP’s most anti-democracy ideas. And Governor Ron DeSantis and his allies are at it again: **Democracy Docket: “With SAVE America Act stalled, Florida House passes its own version”** You've seen the warnings about the most extreme anti-voter bill in a generation, the so-called “SAVE America Act.” Republicans recently passed it in the House and are planning to bring it to the Senate floor for a vote this week. It’s the same bill that Donald Trump says will “guarantee the midterms.” Well, the Florida House just passed its own version, which could make it harder for Floridians to vote. This dangerous bill would require proof of citizenship to register to vote and would require _all_ existing registered voters to certify their citizenship. **Like with its federal counterpart, married women who changed their names, students, and communities of color would particularly face new hurdles to vote under this bill — all to address a fake voter fraud crisis that doesn’t actually exist. ** Peter, these attacks on democracy are popping up in every corner of the country, and we must mobilize to shut them down. Republicans keep proposing anti-voter bills that offer solutions to problems that simply don’t exist. Their sole purpose is to do everything they can to rig the midterms. We can’t let that happen. name: Mary Peltola
subject: Mukluk telegraph
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260316_2.28-j9K&refcode=em20260316-2&t=1001&akid=5618%2E582294%2EqB-nIX ]Mary Peltola

Here’s my
plan for how we win this election:

This is a ground game. This is person-to-person, human-to-human, mukluk
telegraph.

For those in the Lower 48, mukluk telegraph is a saying we have in the
Bush that basically amounts to gossip.

It’s passing along a message through our conversations with one another,
which is the only way information can really spread in some parts of the
Last Frontier!

In a state as vast and rural as ours, there really is no other way to
reach every Alaskan. That’s why it’s so important for us to travel to
their communities and have those person-to-person conversations.

There are 585,000 square miles in this state — bigger than Texas,
California, and Montana combined. And we’re going to criss-cross it in its
entirety.

But to be honest with you, reaching every community will be expensive.

More than 80% of our communities can only be reached by plane, boat or
snow machine. And when we are able to drive, gas up here costs much more
than it does in most of the Lower 48!

But we don’t have another option. I’m running for U.S. Senate to fight for
all Alaskans, and I’m committed to bringing every borough into this fight
with me.

That’s why I’m asking for your support today. We need to take our message
across Alaska, and we can’t do it without your help.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260316_2.28-j9K&refcode=em20260316-2&t=1002&akid=5618%2E582294%2EqB-nIX ]So if you’re with me, please split a donation today between Chris
Pappas and my campaign for U.S. Senate in Alaska. No matter how much
you’re able to contribute, every donation counts because it all adds up
when we chip in together.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260316_2.28-j9K&amount=5&refcode=em20260316-2&t=1021&akid=5618%2E582294%2EqB-nIX ]Donate $5 »

I’m so grateful for your support. Together, we’re going to win this!

Thanks so much,

Mary

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=5618%2E582294%2EqB-nIX

name: Letlow for Louisiana
subject: LETLOW TAKES THE LEAD IN NEW STATEWIDE GOP PRIMARY POLL
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Julia Letlow for Louisiana
body:
Poll shows President Trump’s endorsement is decisive in Louisiana Senate race

| | |
---
| | | | [|
---](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=bf2673c219&e=95355a072c)
| | | | | |
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** March 16, 2026katherine@julialetlow.com
**LETLOW TAKES THE LEAD IN NEW STATEWIDE GOP PRIMARY POLL** _Poll shows President Trump’s endorsement is decisive in Louisiana Senate race_
**BATON ROUGE, La.** — Congresswoman Julia Letlow leads the Republican primary field in a new statewide poll of likely Republican primary voters, despite Bill Cassidy and his Never Trump allies burning through more than $6 million on attack ads against Letlow’s Trump-endorsed campaign for Senate.
The new survey, conducted by Fabrizio, Lee & Associates on March 11-12, shows Letlow leading the full Republican primary ballot with 27 percent, compared to Cassidy’s 26 percent and John Fleming’s 19 percent, with 28 percent undecided.
The poll also shows the power of President Trump’s endorsement in this race.
**Once likely Republican primary voters are informed that President Trump endorsed Julia Letlow, her lead expands dramatically to 48 percent, while Cassidy falls to 19 percent and Fleming receives 14 percent.**
In a head-to-head runoff matchup, Letlow defeats Cassidy by 12 points, 46 percent to 34 percent.
_“This poll reflects what we are hearing from voters all across Louisiana: they want strong conservative leadership that will fight for our state and protect our values. I am honored to have President Trump’s endorsement, and I am grateful for the broad support our campaign is building across Louisiana,”_ **said** **Congresswoman Julia Letlow.**
_“This is a brutal poll for Bill Cassidy. He has burned through millions of dollars on desperate attack ads and is stuck in the mid-20s, while Julia’s support continues to grow thanks to President Trump’s endorsement. That is what happens when Republican voters are given a clear choice between a Trump-endorsed conservative and a senator who impeached President Trump,”_**said Parker Carey, Campaign Manager for Letlow for Senate.**
The results underscore Cassidy’s weakness with Republican primary voters and show that his attacks have failed to stop Letlow’s momentum. Even after months of heavy spending, Cassidy remains stuck in the mid-20s and trails Letlow in both the three-way ballot and a one-on-one runoff.
The Fabrizio, Lee & Associates survey interviewed 600 likely Republican primary voters in Louisiana on March 11-12, 2026. The margin of error is plus or minus 4.0 percentage points.
Polling memo available here:
[https://accountabilityproject.la/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/3-16-26-Louisiana-RPV-Senate-Memo.pdf](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=0e5a2e23bd&e=95355a072c)
**About Julia Letlow:** Julia Letlow is a Republican candidate for the United States Senate and currently represents Louisiana’s Fifth Congressional District in Congress. She serves on the House Appropriations Committee and has President Trump’s complete and total endorsement.

Musk explained: **_“That’s why they want open borders... That’s why some leaders changed their views on borders. That’s the reason—to bring in more people who could affect our systems.”_**

_But the Senate is stalling_ — _**and we can't let that happen.**_

name: Tim Moore
subject: Elites can afford homes. Can your kids?
disclaimer_text: paid for by Friends of Tim Moore
body:
Peter, tonight is it.

Buying a home used to be the most basic part of the American Dream.

Now? It feels out of reach for too many hardworking families in North Carolina — and that's not acceptable.

I just sat down with HUD Secretary Scott Turner, Michael Whatley, the NC Home Builders Association, and housing leaders in Charlotte to talk honestly about what's broken and how we fix it.

The problem is real: not enough homes, too much government red tape, and families getting priced out of neighborhoods they've lived in for generations.

Rents are up. Home prices are up. And Washington keeps making it harder to build. I need to know what YOU are feeling on the ground — before it gets worse. Take our housing survey TODAY! [https://secure.winred.com/friends-of-tim-moore/031626_housing_samoore/?utm_source=Housefile&utm_medium=SA-Email&utm_campaign=03.16.26_Housing_SAMoore&utm_content=Link&recurring=true]

PUT ON THE PRESSURE: RESPOND NOW [https://secure.winred.com/friends-of-tim-moore/031626_housing_samoore/?utm_source=Housefile&utm_medium=SA-Email&utm_campaign=03.16.26_Housing_SAMoore&utm_content=Link&recurring=true]

This isn't just a policy problem. It's YOUR family's future. It's YOUR kids being unable to afford a home in the same town they grew up in. Every month we wait, another family gets priced out.

That's why I'm fighting for the Housing for the 21st Century Act — already passed the House — which cuts the red tape, modernizes outdated HUD programs, and gets more homes built faster.

But the Senate needs to act, and they need to hear the pressure is real. Take the survey NOW — make sure your voice is on record before we take this fight to the Senate. [https://secure.winred.com/friends-of-tim-moore/031626_housing_samoore/?utm_source=Housefile&utm_medium=SA-Email&utm_campaign=03.16.26_Housing_SAMoore&utm_content=Link&recurring=true]

TELL THE SENATE TO ACT: SOUND OFF [https://secure.winred.com/friends-of-tim-moore/031626_housing_samoore/?utm_source=Housefile&utm_medium=SA-Email&utm_campaign=03.16.26_Housing_SAMoore&utm_content=Link&recurring=true]

This takes 60 seconds. Don't sit this one out.

Fighting for you,

Congressman Tim Moore

North Carolina’s 14th District

body:
More than [200 million Americans faced dangerous weather](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAYhJ8Gb1iAsYkHhi7e0rWj9Qd-4r_CJgIalDx95b5CtzuddKf7vq7rFSjScf-EHW0NaT2wlYi1Yl4DYXbYEOqGeYfsth38gaWsSqiJi4FLs3qg-Fp1521AVDh0aKUxg9FKCdltFmAOECY9XgIAhNkNk5eoVZh1kKBMR_ZsE4M0UkghZG-C85dhHEehnZ7hxrRATzXl_jvRUTcM8ZWemHuX9i7ardZHYcMHUwtTS2utd7dyvjhzppZTMrXcIr3fkD136fBUKR2F_xR-pFw3vpNvWCrfEGqDJ_LTMbV02fpHoxipTIZpcd-B4t9u_Resp1W_AQAA__8PMIDM) Monday as blizzards, tornadoes, triple-digit heat, and flooding hit the country simultaneously from coast to coast.

| | |
---
| | |
# Tuesday, March 17, 2026

| **Dear _Flyover_ Reader,**

Three years ago today—on St. Patrick's Day, 2023—we launched _The Flyover_. It was either a result of good luck or pure stubbornness. I'd like to think it was a little of both.

Back then, we had no idea if this thing would work. All we knew was that millions of Americans were tired of being talked down to by legacy media, and we believed a daily news publication focused on facts first (without the usual slanted nonsense) might be worth a shot.

Turns out, you agreed.

In three years, _The Flyover_ has grown from 47 readers on day one to over 4.4 million across all editions, making us one of the largest independent news platforms in the country.

Most people think you need a 50-acre ranch and a heavy-duty range to keep your skills sharp. **They’re wrong.** We’ve decided to clear out a specific corner of our warehouse, and it contains something that bridges the gap between "childhood nostalgia" and "serious survival utility." We are handing out [**100 tactical play kits for FREE**](https://links.tacticalusa.com/a/1534/click/6688/11767687/72977f5328dd0a83813008dec69b0474d4d856fe/79b6c469a4db6f600235c922d1cee6d845494854?ana=InV0bV90ZXJtPVRVU0EgQU0gTGVhZHMmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPVRVU0EgQU0gLSBBaXJzb2Z0ICsgU2xpbmdzaG90IDQgLSAzLzE3ICZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1kcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSI=) today. It’s perfect for draw-stroke practice and comes with nearly 1,000 rounds of "fuel" so you can keep the session going. **The Force Multiplier:** This isn't a toy. It’s a tempered steel, high-velocity tool featuring a professional-grade yoke and arm support. If you ever found yourself needing to put food on the table without making a sound, this is the skill you’d want in your back pocket. **The "Bullseye" Essentials:** We’re including the hardware you need to actually track your progress, so you aren't just making noise—you're making hits. **Why are we doing this?** Honestly? These are taking up space that we need for our 2026 inventory. But more importantly, we know that once you see the quality of what we’re willing to give away for **$0.00** , you’ll remember our name the next time you need serious gear. **The catch?** There are only 100 of these tactical kits available. subject: It’s in my blood
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Bo French Campaign
body:
Texas deserves leaders who know the oil business.
| | | | [](https://link.emails.bofrench.)
---
|
---
| | Dear friend,
Let me say something most politicians in Austin can’t say ---
I actually know this business, and I didn’t hear it from big-wig Austin lobbyists in fancy suits.
I was born into it.
My family has been in the oil business for nearly 80 years. Both of my grandfathers were in the oil business, and my father was in the oil business as a wildcatter. He also owned a successful oil service and oilfield equipment manufacturing business.
And in Midland, my brothers and I run our family office, still fully engaged in the Texas energy industry every single day.
But that’s not all.
_While the political class was busy giving speeches, I was building businesses overseas that protected the world’s largest oil and gas companies from some of the most dangerous threats on the planet - - radical Islamists and Somali pirates._
So when people ask why I’m running for Railroad Commissioner, the answer is simple:
_**Texas deserves someone who knows the oil business inside and out**._
I’m that man for the job. After all, it's in my blood.

---
| | For years, the Railroad Commission has been held back by career politicians who would rather cater to foreign governments than their own constituents.
And Texans are paying the price.
As Railroad Commissioner, I will use my experience to:
* Lower costs for operators
* Increase efficiency
* Streamline permitting
* Pressure the Legislature to reduce taxes on the industry that powers our state and our economy

Because if we want to secure Texas’s future, we must keep Texas energy dominant.
That’s why I’m asking for your support today.
Together, we can launch the next great Texas energy boom.
---

| | **For Texas,**
**Bo French** **Candidate for TX Railroad Commissioner**

| Dear _Flyover_ Reader,

Three years ago today—on St. Patrick's Day, 2023—we launched _The Flyover_. It was either a result of good luck or pure stubbornness. I'd like to think it was a little of both.

Back then, we had no idea if this thing would work. All we knew was that millions of Americans were tired of being talked down to by legacy media, and we believed a daily news publication focused on facts first (without the usual slanted nonsense) might be worth a shot.

Turns out, you agreed.

In three years, _The Flyover_ has grown from 47 readers on day one to over 4.4 million across all editions, making us one of the largest independent news platforms in the country.

name: Rick | Bennett For Governor
subject: Make health care affordable
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
Mainers who are sick or injured deserve a health care system they can count on. It should be affordable, accessible, and stable – no matter where people live or what they do for work.

| | |
---
---
---
Hi Peter -- Mainers have always understood something essential about democracy: that it works best when communities are strong, local decisions matter, and people have the tools to take care of themselves and one another. That spirit of self-reliance – quiet, practical, and grounded – has carried Maine through every chapter of our history. And it must continue to do so. Sadly today, the American Dream – the Maine Dream – is out of reach for too many families. The cost of living has become unsustainable for too many Mainers, such that many can no longer afford to stay here, work here, raise families here, and plan for the future with confidence. A Maine where families have to check their bank account before seeing a doctor – and choose between filling a prescription or filling their oil tank – is a state with a failing economic model. **Addressing Maine’s health care affordability demands a seriousness and urgency to meet the moment.** That is why yesterday, I announced our health care affordability plan, which includes four priorities:
* Demand results and transparency from State programs
* Invest in health: a prevention-first approach to lowering costs
* Launch the medical debt relief program
* Commit to a path to universal care for every Mainer

[The details matter, of course, and you can read my plan by clicking here.](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=gbTKlsDTP6xWO2908dmfEDyaMdDQ7esxCA3vZIOo4k1Iziun55uTopUQrmFabn60j7cTK2GpATeSkQpE-uPWovhuCJ8wDoDiCZRBBgUW9xjhnqcJI52vJeU6uZ8Nvdwk-CilWE5k9Fitp1AV4Og0GHVsm3GQn9E8xxR5XPsZ1YWGiAgQiOReUMl6PQ6c1SwnsGA3CCHgKeSb_dTf2x_gUw&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=health_care&n=1)

Mainers who are sick or injured deserve a health care system they can count on. It should be affordable, accessible, and stable – no matter where people live or what they do for work.

Let’s get to work. Rick Bennett

[P.S. If you agree with me that Maine’s next Governor needs to be focused on the issues that matter most, please consider chipping in $25, $50, or $100 today to help us get there.](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/donate?e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=health_care&n=2)

All of the talking heads are talking about the House and Senate elections, and yes, those will be consequential. But here's the truth most political pundits and election analysts are missing:
The fate of Democracy will also hinge on often overlooked and underappreciated state Supreme Courts races.
As MAGA witnessed the formation of a massive blue wave in 2025, they started working on desperate countermeasures, launching an all-out blitz of anti-democratic election rigging efforts at the state level--rewriting elections laws to make it harder for Democrats to vote and gerrymandering maps.
The constitutionality of their actions will ultimately be decided by state Supreme Courts. That means whoever controls these courts will control the fate of our Democracy:

body:
After that, you can go on with your day!
Can we have a quick chat? I promise it'll be brief.
I need your attention for just two minutes. After that, you can go on with your day:

subject: 10 Paradoxes of Our Age
body:
Have you noticed how our world seems full of contradictions lately?

| | | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z0d3tpp09ou75ldomdolv07oau7aldq82bdec488_rp22sh2s8i6epr6cthmap74cth2bs)
---
| | Dear Friend,

Have you noticed how our world seems full of contradictions lately?
Prosperity is rising. Yet freedom, in many places, is retreating.

Global diplomacy expands. But so do threats.

Cultural traditions persist. Still, they're strained by mass migration and ideological division.
---
|
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z0b7isj31mjprrnasrg32ab9on1evigjrgji40f0_rp22sh2s8i6epr6cthmap74cth2bs)
---
| | These aren't just abstract concepts--they're reshaping the world we live in right now.

And if we don't understand them, we risk misunderstanding the forces at work and misjudging our response.

That's why the Hoover Institution is sharing a **powerful new analysis from Senior Fellow Victor Davis Hanson:_Ten Paradoxes of Our Age_.**

In it, he outlines ten defining paradoxes of our time, including:
* Why economic growth doesn't always bring political freedom
* How diplomacy can coexist with rising global insecurity
* What happens when cultural pressures outpace integration

Whether you're concerned about America's future role in the world or seeking clarity amid global confusion, this piece offers a timely perspective.

These paradoxes are reshaping our world, and understanding them is crucial.

"If we do not understand the paradoxes of our age, we will continue to be confused by the outcomes." -- Victor Davis Hanson

name: Wes Climer
subject: Judicial Reform Is About the Integrity of the System
body:
Dear Friends

America's founders believed deeply in the separation of powers. The
legislature writes the laws. The executive enforces them. The judiciary
interprets them. Each branch has its role and each branch serves as a check
on the others. South Carolina's current system for selecting judges blurs
those lines in ways that should concern anyone who cares about the
integrity of the courts or their own freedoms.

South Carolina remains one of only two states in the country where the
legislature effectively controls the judicial selection process from
beginning to end. The General Assembly appoints the members of the Judicial
Merit Selection Commission. That commission screens judicial candidates.
The legislature then elects the judges.

When the same branch of government manages each step of that process, the
result is an extraordinary concentration of authority in one place.

Many legislators serve with great integrity and take their responsibilities
seriously. But structure matters. Systems should be designed to avoid
conflicts of interest and preserve public confidence. In South Carolina,
lawyer-legislators routinely appear in court before judges who were
screened and elected through a process the legislature controls. Even when
everyone involved acts honorably, that arrangement raises understandable
questions for the public.

Justice must not only be fair. It must also be seen to be fair. That is why
judicial reform has become an important conversation in our state. The
legislation currently under consideration would move South Carolina toward
a system that more closely resembles the constitutional balance of power
envisioned by our founders.

Under the proposal, the governor would appoint the members of the Judicial
Merit Selection Commission. The commission would continue to vet candidates
and evaluate their qualifications. The General Assembly would still elect
judges. But the legislature would no longer control the entire pipeline.
Authority would be distributed rather than concentrated.

That is not a radical idea. In fact, it would bring South Carolina closer
to the model used by most states in the country.

Some have argued that we should pause and see how recently enacted changes
to the judicial screening process perform before pursuing additional
reforms. But we were given a real-world reminder of the system’s weaknesses
in just the last couple weeks.

The former Speaker of the South Carolina House nearly secured a seat on the
South Carolina Supreme Court despite having very little experience as a
judge. Regardless of anyone’s view of the individuals involved, that
episode highlighted a broader structural problem. When legislative
relationships and internal politics become central to judicial selection,
the system begins to look less like a search for the best legal minds and
more like an extension of the political process.

That is not healthy for the judiciary and it is not healthy for public
trust.

The goal of reform is not to criticize those who have served under the
current system. It is to strengthen the system itself. Institutions endure
when they are willing to improve.

At its core, judicial reform is about humility. It is about recognizing
that no branch of government should accumulate too much authority over
time. It is about remembering that the purpose of constitutional design is
to prevent power from becoming too comfortable in any one place and
threatening the freedoms of the citizens.

The Senate now has an opportunity to continue the work the House has
already begun. Many Senate Republicans understand the importance of this
issue and support moving the bill forward. Yet, like many conservative
reforms over the years, the legislation currently sits stuck in committee.

Committees are meant to study legislation, not quietly bury it. Judicial
reform deserves to be debated openly on the Senate floor so that every
member can vote according to his or her judgment.

South Carolina has an opportunity to strengthen one of its most important
institutions. The courts function best when they are independent of
political influence and when the public can trust that independence.

Reforming the judicial selection process will not solve every problem
overnight. But it will move us toward a system that better reflects the
principles of separation of powers, judicial independence and public
accountability.

That is a goal worthy of bipartisan support and serious consideration.

Thank you for your support,

— Wes Climer

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | 3 Dividend Stocks to Buy and Hold Forever (for a lifetime of income) I've dug through the over 3,000 dividend stocks on the market to pinpoint I expect them to increase their dividend payouts in the years to come... so BUYING NOW means you could be picking up shares at an amazing price. [**The SAVE America Act is being pushed to strip away at our democracy and put up barriers to the ballot box. We must protect the right to vote – not restrict it. | | Friend, Despite the obvious clues that something wasn’t right in Minnesota, the mainstream media – in their typical fashion – intentionally ignored what eventually became one of the year’s biggest stories. Even when reports about massive fraud tied to taxpayer-funded childcare programs started surfacing, _most legacy outlets barely touched it._ The story was complicated, politically uncomfortable, and easy for the national media to quietly overlook. **But independent journalist Nick Shirley didn’t overlook it.** He grabbed a camera, went to the locations reported to be receiving taxpayer money, knocked on doors, and documented what he found: Facilities receiving large sums of taxpayer funding that appeared empty. Serious questions about where the money was actually going. And a story that suddenly millions of Americans couldn’t ignore. His investigation _exploded_ online. Members of Congress started asking questions. And a scandal that had been quietly buried was forced into the national spotlight. **That’s the power of independent journalism, and it’s exactly why Lincoln Media Foundation exists.** Lincoln Media Foundation (LMF) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to exposing media bias and making sure critical stories don’t disappear just because powerful institutions would rather they did. We fund independent journalism, partner with citizen reporters, and use a growing digital media network to amplify stories the mainstream press ignores. **[Right now, that includes supporting Nick Shirley and the investigative work he’s continuing across the country.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | [ HELP LMF SUPPORT NICK SHIRLEY ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | After exposing the Minnesota scandal, Nick has taken his investigations to California, examining government programs, visiting publicly funded facilities, auditing voter roles, and documenting the kinds of questions legacy media are not only refusing to ask, _but condemning him for pursuing._ **He goes where others won’t.** **He asks the questions others avoid.** **And he shows the public what he finds.** But investigations like this take real resources — travel, filming, editing, publishing, distribution, and – in Nick’s case – _even security_. Independent journalists don’t have billion-dollar newsrooms behind them. On top of this, the mainstream media, leftist politicians, and the corrupt individuals Nick is exposing are all working to discredit him and bury the harsh truths he is uncovering. **That’s why Lincoln Media Foundation is asking for your help today. Without support from people like you, Nick won’t be able to continue his work.** **[Your tax-deductible gift of $10, $25, $50, or more will help LMF directly support Nick Shirley’s investigative work — helping him continue exposing stories the mainstream media ignores and making sure millions of Americans see the truth.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D

Dear Patriot,

You know it and I know it -- Congress is broken.

Politicians have turned “serving the people” into “serving themselves.” They use their positions to get richer and richer every year, while you and I get left behind.

Left-wing radicals like Ilhan Omar, Rashida Tlaib, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez work to destroy our country from within. And Washington never fixes anything.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D
Today, WE THE PEOPLE have a chance to do something about it when you sign your “Time for Term Limits” petition and submit it in the next 72 hours.

Our Founding Fathers never intended for government service to be a permanent career. George Washington famously served just two terms — then went home.

Our Founding Fathers also said our government was made for a “moral and religious people.”

And they understood that if that moral compass broke down, Congress could easily steer America in the wrong direction, become a do-nothing body, or make government a gravy train for themselves.

That’s why they included a powerful safeguard in our Constitution -- an escape hatch -- enshrined in Article V.

If Congress ever became too corrupt to fix itself, Article V. says the states can use this provision in the Constitution to act.

34 state legislatures can call a convention, propose term limits -- and Congress can’t do a thing about it.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D
Here at AMAC Action, we have led the term limits movement in the past, and we are ready to put our efforts behind the movement once again.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D
Time for Term Limits

My friend, can you imagine Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez spending 30 more years in Congress??

We are AMAC Action. “AMAC” stands for Association of Mature American Citizens. And when it comes to standing up for the rights of Americans, “action” is what we’re known for.

President Trump has said that AMAC Action is so effective that members of Congress run the other way when they see our delegates coming down the hall.

And our “Time for Term Limits” Petition Drive certainly has Washington lifers on the run!

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D
Please sign your petition and submit it in the next 72 hours.

>> No more golden pensions for people who work 170 days a year and spend half of that just trying to get reelected.

>> No more using the power of the office to destroy American values from within.

>> No more insider deals to get rich.

>> No more jobs for life with nothing to show for it!

Some of these grifters and America-haters have been “working” in Congress over 30, and even 40 years!

- Maxine Waters — 34 years
- Chuck Schumer — 44 years
- Patty Murray — 33 years

They’ve been in the swamp so long they’ve grown gills.

Please – let’s not let them drag America down into the swamp with them. It’s time to use the escape hatch our Founders left for us.

34 state legislatures are needed. What will embolden states to act is seeing a massive groundswell of support for term limits from millions of Americans just like you.

That’s why AMAC Action is spearheading this massive 50-state Petition Drive and why you got my email today.

You’ve proven that you’re a patriot who can be counted on to take action.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D
Please sign your “Time for Term Limits” petition and submit it in the next 72 hours with your sacrificial donation of $35, $50 or more to spread this national campaign across America.

We need to reach 1 million patriots with petitions just like yours.

And that takes time and money.

The Washington lifers are counting on having more power, influence, and resources than the American people.

They’re counting on our complacency and despair.

But here at AMAC Action we say: Let’s finish the fight our Founders began and restore America’s government to the people.

Your $35 gift is enough to send and collect 50 more “Time for Term Limits” petitions across email, text, and mail. Your gift of $70 funds 100 more “Time for Term Limits” petitions.

Singlehandedly, you are an indispensable force-multiplier in this effort.

But if you do nothing, nothing changes.

- Immigration policy will never get fixed and just stay a meaningless election year talking point.
- America’s spending and debt will continue to grow unchecked. Remember when we had a balanced budget? We can get back there if career politicians do something!
- Social Security will keep getting raided while real policies to protect your benefits sit on the back burner.

He's removing distractions, confirming promises, and aligning hearts with their divine assignments like never before. It's a wake-up call full of hope, direction, and supernatural clarity! In today's episode of **The Rachel Hamm Show** I'll share the entire dream, the interpretation the Holy Spirit gave me, and the steps He's leading us to take in response. This isn't theory—it's fresh revelation straight from Heaven, and I believe it will stir something deep in your spirit.

Join me TODAY, March 17th @ 8:30AM Pacific Watch or listen here:

Many of you have messaged me saying you're in a season of transition or questioning your purpose... I truly believe this word is part of the answer. After you watch, comment on the video—I'd love to hear what God highlights to you personally. Your testimonies encourage me and the whole community! Praying the Holy Spirit illuminates your path even more brightly!
For God & Country,

body:
I traveled to New York for a deposition that was seven months in the making

| | | | | [|
---](https://ericburlisonforcongress.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b6500a115da3c4344522b1e48&id=92026458d4&e=5f9dc01b8c)
| | Peter ,

I never thought I’d be sitting across the table from Hillary Clinton asking her questions about Jeffrey Epstein. But last week, that’s exactly what happened.For nearly seven months, my team and I prepared for a deposition that most people in Washington didn’t think would ever happen. We issued a bipartisan subpoena, supported by both Republicans and Democrats, calling on about two dozen powerful people who were connected to Jeffrey Epstein.Every single one cooperated. Except the Clintons. We were on the verge of holding them in contempt of Congress before they finally agreed.When I got Hillary Clinton under oath, the facts I laid out were damning. Jeffrey Epstein visited the Clinton White House 17 times. He donated $20,000 to Hillary. Ghislaine Maxwell hosted a fundraiser for her. Maxwell attended Chelsea Clinton’s wedding, skipping a DOJ deposition to be there. Maxwell even told investigators she’d stop by the Clinton home in Chappaqua when she was in the area.Hillary’s response to nearly all of it? “I don’t recall.”She deflected. # **Senior Iranian leader who warned Trump 'watch out for yourself' killed in Israeli strike**
Ali Larijani, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council who warned President Donald Trump last week to "watch out for yourself -- lest you be eliminated," **[was killed in an overnight strike](https://substack.com/redirect/dcda719e-d59f-4aa8-8959-17f01fad247b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** along with Gen. Gholam Reza Soleimani, head of the Revolutionary Guard's Basij force. The 67-year-old Larijani was one of 10 Iranian officials with a $10 million State Department bounty and had told a TV interviewer days earlier that Trump "doesn't understand that the Iranian nation is mature and determined."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcda719e-d59f-4aa8-8959-17f01fad247b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said "Larijani and the Basij commander were eliminated last night and have joined [Ayatollah Ali] Khamenei, the head of the annihilation program, along with all those eliminated from the axis of evil in the depths of hell." Netanyahu's office posted an image of him on the phone Tuesday "ordering the elimination of senior Iranian regime officials." Larijani was sanctioned in January for coordinating violent suppression of protests that killed thousands, with the IDF saying Basij forces under Soleimani "led key suppression operations involving severe violence, widespread arrests, and the use of force against civilian protesters."
* **The backdrop:** The strikes deal another blow to Iran's theocracy following the Feb. 28 killing of Ali Khamenei, amid intense speculation about successor Mojtaba Khamenei's health and whereabouts. Larijani had responded Sunday to his $10 million bounty by quoting early Shia Islam leader Hussein Ibn Ali: "I do not see death as anything but happiness." After Trump threatened attacks over the Strait of Hormuz closure, Larijani wrote "Iran does not fear your paper threats" and "even those greater than you could not eliminate the Iranian nation."

* * *
# **80% of DHS terrorism investigators working without pay during government shutdown amid Iran conflict**
Eighty percent of the Department of Homeland Security's Office of Intelligence & Analysis--the primary office tracking terrorism and threats--**[is working without pay due to the ongoing partial government shutdown,](https://substack.com/redirect/cd81e598-a9d2-4cd8-8b29-eaccbe1c4194?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with DHS not funded since February 14. A DHS spokesman told The Daily Wire "Democrats are shamelessly playing politics with national security" as the agency faces increased importance following at least four attacks on Americans since the Iran conflict began.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cd81e598-a9d2-4cd8-8b29-eaccbe1c4194?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** President Trump said "the Democrats are terrible...we're fighting big battles with a very tough enemy...and we're not allowed to have security in our country." The shutdown also means TSA workers have gone without paychecks for weeks, causing staffing shortages and incredibly long security lines, while FEMA, the Coast Guard, and thousands of federal law enforcement officers lack pay and resources. With major events like America 250 and the World Cup approaching, DHS needs full funding "to ensure the safety and security of the homeland."
* **The recent attacks:** The four attacks include a Michigan synagogue ramming by Ayman Mohamad Ghazali; an Old Dominion University shooting by former National Guard soldier Mohamed Bailor Jalloh, previously convicted of supporting ISIS; two ISIS-inspired suspects attempting to detonate explosives near NYC Mayor Mamdani's home; and an Austin, Texas bar shooting by a gunman wearing a "Property of Allah" hoodie that killed three. Former special presidential envoy Nathan Sales warned "if you're a Hezbollah operative and you want to carry out an attack in the United States, you have to cross the border, and that's a DHS responsibility."

* * *
# **Minneapolis sees 35% surge in auto thefts as Walz, Frey blame ICE operations instead of crime policies**
Minneapolis reported **[over 1,000 auto thefts](https://substack.com/redirect/54057b6d-a414-4c44-8eaf-c3394421cda0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in January and February 2026--a nearly 35% increase compared to the same period last year--with the trend continuing into March, including at least 20 thefts on March 14 alone. Gov. Tim Walz and Mayor Jacob Frey have blamed federal ICE operations, with Police Chief Brian O'Hara suggesting Trump's Operation Metro Surge was a "contributing factor" because "officers and investigators were consistently pulled from their normal assigned duties."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eac929fa-657f-4d2b-a236-9f61a5a171a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Car thefts in Minneapolis in January and February 2026 reported by Crime Watch Minneapolis
* **Why it matters:** Retired Minnesota State Patrol Lt. John Nagel, running for Congress against Rep. Ilhan Omar, told Fox News Digital "this isn't an ICE problem. It's a deterrence problem," noting St. Paul saw car theft drop sharply with "focused enforcement" while Minneapolis hit 1,000 thefts in two months. He blamed Walz and Frey for "making excuses, undermining deterrence, and tolerating a revolving door for repeat offenders--especially juveniles," saying the city needs "more officers, proactive policing, prosecutors willing to act, and a juvenile system with the capacity to intervene."
* **The challenges:** The Minneapolis Police Department acknowledged it "continues to be understaffed" after losing 40% of its ranks since George Floyd's death in 2020 and has a policy to "not pursue stolen vehicles." County Attorney Mary Moriarty's spokesperson said motor vehicle thefts are "really tough for police to solve" with only 3% resulting in arrests, making "deterrence much less likely," though a mid-2023 initiative reportedly led to a 58% drop in teen car theft cases.

| A new survey of likely Republican primary voters released today shows Congresswoman Nancy Mace firmly leading the field in the 2026 South Carolina governor’s race, and widening her advantage as the campaign heats up.

The Stratus Intelligence survey, conducted from March 9-11, 2026, shows Mace leading the Republican primary field with 24% of likely voters, six points ahead of the nearest competitor. But the topline number only tells part of the story. Since Stratus’s January survey, Mace’s favorability climbed from 34% to 42%, while unfavorability went down. She is the only candidate in the field trending in the right direction. The other candidates have each seen their unfavorability increase as more voters get to know them, a troubling trajectory heading into the final stretch of the primary. **The ballot stands as follows:** • Nancy Mace: 24% • Alan Wilson: 18% • Pamela Evette: 15% • Ralph Norman: 14% • Undecided: 29% “Mace’s high favorability, strong standing, and positive trajectory place her in the best position to consolidate additional support while the rest of the field is stuck vying for second place.” **\- Clare Considine, Director of Polling at Stratus Intelligence**

name: Senator Dick Anderson
subject: Sine Die Update and Town Hall Announcement
body:
Senator Anderson Legislative Newsletter
---
| | | [](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fcontent.govdelivery.com%2Faccounts%2FORLEG%2Fbulletins%2F40e2db5/1/0101019cfc45bdc0-92b2cf3d-09e7-436b-aca4-c2858d9c788b-000000/9705jaAkQhYzre3_FvoKhvqzPwzentbbUAI3ZZ78nM0=448 "View Online")
---|---
---
**Dear Friends and Neighbors of District 5,** Dear Friends and Neighbors, The 2026 Regular Session of the Oregon Legislative Assembly concluded on Friday, March 6, 2026, after convening on February 2nd. This 35-day short session brought more than 260 bills before the chamber on issues ranging from housing and transportation funding to data privacy, school finance, and responses to federal policy changes. I’m honored to serve in leadership positions that connect your priorities to the heart of the legislative process. This session, I continued as **Vice-Chair of the Senate Committee on Early Childhood and Behavioral Health** and **Vice-Chair of the Senate Committee on Housing and Development** —two committees directly focused on key issues affecting families across District 5. I also served as **Co-Chair of the Senate Committee on Conduct and the Joint Committee on Conduct** , and as a member of the **Senate Committee on Finance and Revenue** , the **Joint Committee on Ways and Means.** These assignments give District 5 a voice in shaping policy across a broad range of issues. **Your Input Matters!** **Please join me for a townhall in Coos Bay- Thursday, March 19 from 12- 1 pm at Southwestern Oregon Community College- Tioga Hall, Room 505.** Looking forward to seeing you there, **Senator Dick Anderson**
Oregon State Senate, District 5 |
* * *
---
As Vice-Chair of the Housing and Development Committee, I continue to serve as Senate Republicans' lead voice on housing policy — a role I have embraced since joining the Legislature in 2021. During the short session, we passed some good legislation further cutting red tape for communities to bring in land into the UGB. There was also another bill focused on land for 55+ communities to be built if cities wanted more land to serve our fastest growing demographic in Oregon. Probably not the demographic we want to lead in, but none the less, it is needed.
As Vice-Chair of the Senate Committee on Early Childhood and Behavioral Health, I am helping guide legislation aimed at strengthening Oregon’s behavioral health workforce and addressing barriers in our child care system. Coastal communities continue to face provider shortages and limited access to care, and our committee’s work this session was focused on AI in behavioral health (SB1546) and Child Care liability (SB1535).
My work on the Senate Committee on Finance and Revenue and the Joint Committee on Ways and Means places me at the center of state budget discussions. This session, we addressed way to much for a 35 day short session. There were bills on federal disconnect, estate taxes, transient room lodging tax, new banking regulations, tax credits and many more very large issues. I am looking forward to doing some more work in the long session to modify our tax system in Oregon.
The short session timeline means decisions moved quickly, and I remained committed to representing District 5’s priorities in every committee room and every vote.
# Rural Oregon Victories and Big Bills
This session delivered significant support for rural communities, agriculture, and natural resources, including one of my own, Senate Bill 1535.
SB 1535 — Childcare: This bill directs the Department of Early Learning and Care (DELC) to take several steps aimed at improving Oregon's child care system. It allows the Early Learning Council to modify eligibility priorities for the Employment Related Day Care subsidy program, giving it flexibility in how families receiving temporary assistance for needy families are prioritized. It also requires DELC to conduct a broader study of childcare in Oregon and to convene a workgroup to examine the cost and availability of liability insurance for childcare providers and explore strategies to increase access, reduce financial burdens, and address related liability challenges. This is a win for working families in Oregon and I am proud to have sponsored this bill.
Philomath Housing infrastructure dollars secured. My top funding priority was for the City of Philomath for $2.65 million to upgrade the sewer connections to help unlock new housing to be built faster. We worked with the City of Philomath to ensure this funding was included.
Bay Area Hospital - HB 4075 was passed to help with Hospital funding in Coos Bay. This funding package allowed for $44 million dollars in backed funds to help the hospital reorganize its debt with the backing of the state.
HB 4153 — Farm Stores: Expands options for farm-based retail operations. We have to give our farms more tools to secure revenue or we will continue to lose them. I was a Chief Sponsor on this legislation.
SB 1601 — Lottery Funds for County Fairgrounds: Removes the cap on 1% of lottery proceeds going to county fairgrounds, effective July 1, 2027. Fairgrounds around the state have been dealing with crumbling infrastructure needs for years, this was a good win for our rural counties.
Horse Racing Support: $5 million allocated to Crook, Harney, Josephine, Tillamook, and Union counties. Along, with the fairgrounds, securing some revenue for major events like horse racing, will keep this counties vibrant and moving forward.
HB 4134 — Increases the Transient Lodging Tax (TLT) statewide from 1.5% to 2.25%. The new 1.25% increment is dedicated to:
* Oregon Conservation Corps funding
* Wolf Management Compensation (additional $1m added)
* Wildlife connectivity and stewardship
* Anti-poaching and wildlife law enforcement
* Invasive species control

HB 4148 — changes the TLT local government tourism promotion revenue split from 30/70 to 50/50 if a county chooses to do it. This allows for local control over how they want to see their revenue being used in the community.
FFA Funding: Held harmless in this session's budget.
Outdoor School: Funding protected.
Education: No cuts to the top-line education budget; however, some school districts face hardship due to multiple years of declining enrollment.
# Housing
SB 1566 — Making Affordable Housing Pencil: I brought SB 1566 to the Labor and Business committee at the beginning of the session after hearing that affordable housing projects were stalling out or being shelved all together because of the way a rule was being interpreted and implemented by BOLI. This bill was an effort to reduce construction cost for affordable housing projects and was met with swift opposition from Labor Unions, however public support for this bill was robust. This bill would have cut red tape, making it less expensive to build homes that lower-income Oregonians can afford- instead this bill died in committee, proving the power of the Big Labor Unions. We are glad to hear there is talks ongoing with Oregon Housing and BOLI to get better clarification on prevailing wage for affordable housing.
HB 4120 — Residential Tenancy: Allows landlords to ban smoking in residential tenancies, giving property owners a new tool to protect buildings and other tenants.
HB 4035 — Urban Growth Boundary Fixes: Technical fixes to SB 1537 (2024) streamlines the Urban Growth Boundary (UGB) expansion process:
* Removed the "severely rent-burdened" threshold cities must display to trigger the land use expansion process.
* Cities must not have large undeveloped internal tracts (20+ net residential acres) to qualify.
* Resource lands may be used when they make up 80% of land surrounding the UGB within a quarter mile.
* Cities over 25,000 population may expand by up to 150 net residential acres (increased from 100 acres under SB 1537).

HB 4082 — One-time UGB Expansion for Seniors: Allows cities of 25,000 or more to bring in up to 100 acres, and smaller cities up to 50 acres, for a one-time UGB expansion. _This tool is restricted to housing that benefits people aged 55 and older._
HB 4037 — Housing Omnibus: A broad package of housing reforms including:
* City and County Housing Project Funding: Technical fixes to the Moderate-Income Revolving Loan Program to make homeownership development more feasible.
* CDFI Predevelopment Loans: Expands project eligibility and funding amounts under the Moderate-Income Housing Predevelopment Loan Program.
* Housing Enforcement: Fixes a technical error that had limited enforcement orders to cities above 10,000 population.
* Building Plan Self-Certification: Expands to engineered and non-prescriptive building plans.
* Housing Application Review: Requires applications meeting clear and objective standards to be processed without an initial public hearing; limits land use appeals to the applicant.
* Disaster Tenancy Protections: Creates standards for tenant access, obligations, and rights to rented units after a natural disaster.
* Surplus State Land for Housing: Clarifies priority order for acquiring surplus state lands for affordable and market-rate housing development.

SB 1561 — Natural Disaster Rebuilding: Makes it easier to rebuild a home after a natural disaster. This is a significant bill as there was groups looking to not allow home owners to rebuild after their house was destroyed in rural parts of Oregon.
# Public Safety
HB 4145 —Measure 114 Delay: Pushes back the implementation of Measure 114 to January 1, 2028, while the Oregon Supreme Court completes its ruling on the case. This turned into a good gun bill from a bad one.
There were a number of "anti police" bills that passed on partisan lines. I am very concerned about ongoing erosion of respect for law enforcement in our country. We must have order to be a nation, our police are tasked with keeping things in order on both the local and national level. We have laws, they enforce them. There is a process and it just feels like the majority party just wants to use our police as political pawns, I don't like it.
# Taxes & Fiscal Policy
HB 4125 & SJR 201 (DEFEATED)—Protecting the Kicker: Both bills that would have modified Oregon's kicker tax rebate were successfully killed, protecting taxpayers' rebates.
SB 1511 — Estate Tax (DEFEATED): The defeat of Senate Bill 1511 is a win for Oregon Taxpayers, while the bill raised the exemption threshold, it simultaneously imposed some of the highest estate tax rates in the nation topping out at nearly 20%. This bill would have severe repercussions for successful small business owners, farmers, and entrepreneurs that would have faced an even steeper tax burden at death. Oregon already struggles to retain high net worth residents and imposing near record tax rates would only accelerate that exodus, ultimately costing the state income tax revenue, jobs and investment. By defeating this bill the legislature has the opportunity to go back to the drawing board and pursue estate tax reform that truly protects Oregon families, keeps generational businesses intact, and makes the state a more attractive place to live, work and build a legacy.
SB 1507 — Federal Tax Disconnect: Raises taxes by approximately $300 million while offering an extremely limited $25 million tax credit in return. This bill remains a significant concern for Oregon businesses and families.
HB 4098 (DEFEATED) —Insurance Cost Protection: Would have raised insurance prices, was successfully killed for another year — continuing a decade-long effort to protect Oregonians from higher insurance costs.
# Economic Development
HB 4084 — Governor's Prosperity Bill, designed to boost Oregon's economic competitiveness:
* Fast-track permitting in limited circumstances
* Funding for industrial site readiness
* Enterprise zone program improvements One-year moratorium on using enterprise zones for data centers

SB 1586 — from Senator Sollman, (DID NOT PASS). It would have brought 1,700 acres into Hillsboro's UGB for advanced manufacturing and semiconductor development, expanded Oregon's R&D tax credit, created an optional local property tax waiver for new machinery and equipment in advanced manufacturing.
SB 1501 — Legislation related to the Moda Center and the Portland Trail Blazers organization passed this session. Details to follow as implementation proceeds.
# Recreation & Liability
HB 1517 — Generally makes liability waivers enforceable for recreational activities. However, the bill contains several exemptions that limit how much it can reduce costs for recreation businesses and operators.
# Campaign Finance
HB 4018 — Makes important technical fixes to Oregon's recently adopted campaign finance law. Contribution limits for state legislative campaigns take effect January 1, 2027. I am for new campaign finance legislation, however I also think we need an overhaul on our systems and the best way to curb corruption is to put term limits on legislators in effect.
# Transportation
SB 1599 — Gas tax measure: Moves the gas tax ballot measure election to the May election cycle.
* * *
---
District 5 continues to be full of community energy!
A major milestone worth celebrating in southern Lincoln County was the **official grand opening and ribbon-cutting for the new Yachats Public Library,** a modern, expanded facility that replaced the original 1973 structure. The new library features increased space for books and community resources, a larger children’s area, public computers, and a community room — marking a significant investment in lifelong learning and community gathering in Yachats.
Looking ahead, there are several upcoming opportunities for engagement and community participation across the district. The **Oregon Coast Council for the Arts** in Newport has planned spring and early summer performances and exhibitions, while the calendar of events in Yachats includes arts and crafts fairs, cultural gatherings, and recreational activities that highlight the unique coastal character of our communities.
These events reflect the rich cultural and civic life of District 5 — from library celebrations and festivals to arts, learning, and community gatherings. I am grateful to be a part of such a vibrant community.
The connection between **people** and their **governmen** t is bolstered when the public has **substantial opportunity** to let their concerns be heard by their elected officials. Below are a few ways that **YOU** can join in on the**legislative process.**
