clean_body: Senator Anderson Legislative Newsletter | | | "View Online" ---|--- Dear Friends and Neighbors of District 5, Dear Friends and Neighbors, The 2026 Regular Session of the Oregon Legislative Assembly concluded on Friday, March 6, 2026, after convening on February 2nd. This 35-day short session brought more than 260 bills before the chamber on issues ranging from housing and transportation funding to data privacy, school finance, and responses to federal policy changes. I’m honored to serve in leadership positions that connect your priorities to the heart of the legislative process. This session, I continued as Vice-Chair of the Senate Committee on Early Childhood and Behavioral Health and Vice-Chair of the Senate Committee on Housing and Development —two committees directly focused on key issues affecting families across District 5. I also served as Co-Chair of the Senate Committee on Conduct and the Joint Committee on Conduct , and as a member of the Senate Committee on Finance and Revenue , the Joint Committee on Ways and Means. These assignments give District 5 a voice in shaping policy across a broad range of issues. Your Input Matters! Please join me for a townhall in Coos Bay- Thursday, March 19 from 12- 1 pm at Southwestern Oregon Community College- Tioga Hall, Room 505. Looking forward to seeing you there, Senator Dick Anderson Oregon State Senate, District 5 | As Vice-Chair of the Housing and Development Committee, I continue to serve as Senate Republicans' lead voice on housing policy — a role I have embraced since joining the Legislature in 2021. During the short session, we passed some good legislation further cutting red tape for communities to bring in land into the UGB. There was also another bill focused on land for 55+ communities to be built if cities wanted more land to serve our fastest growing demographic in Oregon. Probably not the demographic we want to lead in, but none the less, it is needed. As Vice-Chair of the Senate Committee on Early Childhood and Behavioral Health, I am helping guide legislation aimed at strengthening Oregon’s behavioral health workforce and addressing barriers in our child care system. Coastal communities continue to face provider shortages and limited access to care, and our committee’s work this session was focused on AI in behavioral health (SB1546) and Child Care liability (SB1535). My work on the Senate Committee on Finance and Revenue and the Joint Committee on Ways and Means places me at the center of state budget discussions. This session, we addressed way to much for a 35 day short session. There were bills on federal disconnect, estate taxes, transient room lodging tax, new banking regulations, tax credits and many more very large issues. I am looking forward to doing some more work in the long session to modify our tax system in Oregon. The short session timeline means decisions moved quickly, and I remained committed to representing District 5’s priorities in every committee room and every vote. Rural Oregon Victories and Big Bills This session delivered significant support for rural communities, agriculture, and natural resources, including one of my own, Senate Bill 1535. SB 1535 — Childcare: This bill directs the Department of Early Learning and Care (DELC) to take several steps aimed at improving Oregon's child care system. It allows the Early Learning Council to modify eligibility priorities for the Employment Related Day Care subsidy program, giving it flexibility in how families receiving temporary assistance for needy families are prioritized. It also requires DELC to conduct a broader study of childcare in Oregon and to convene a workgroup to examine the cost and availability of liability insurance for childcare providers and explore strategies to increase access, reduce financial burdens, and address related liability challenges. This is a win for working families in Oregon and I am proud to have sponsored this bill. Philomath Housing infrastructure dollars secured. My top funding priority was for the City of Philomath for $2.65 million to upgrade the sewer connections to help unlock new housing to be built faster. We worked with the City of Philomath to ensure this funding was included. Bay Area Hospital - HB 4075 was passed to help with Hospital funding in Coos Bay. This funding package allowed for $44 million dollars in backed funds to help the hospital reorganize its debt with the backing of the state. HB 4153 — Farm Stores: Expands options for farm-based retail operations. We have to give our farms more tools to secure revenue or we will continue to lose them. I was a Chief Sponsor on this legislation. SB 1601 — Lottery Funds for County Fairgrounds: Removes the cap on 1% of lottery proceeds going to county fairgrounds, effective July 1, 2027. Fairgrounds around the state have been dealing with crumbling infrastructure needs for years, this was a good win for our rural counties. Horse Racing Support: $5 million allocated to Crook, Harney, Josephine, Tillamook, and Union counties. Along, with the fairgrounds, securing some revenue for major events like horse racing, will keep this counties vibrant and moving forward. HB 4134 — Increases the Transient Lodging Tax (TLT) statewide from 1.5% to 2.25%. The new 1.25% increment is dedicated to: Oregon Conservation Corps funding Wolf Management Compensation (additional $1m added) Wildlife connectivity and stewardship Anti-poaching and wildlife law enforcement Invasive species control HB 4148 — changes the TLT local government tourism promotion revenue split from 30/70 to 50/50 if a county chooses to do it. This allows for local control over how they want to see their revenue being used in the community. FFA Funding: Held harmless in this session's budget. Outdoor School: Funding protected. Education: No cuts to the top-line education budget; however, some school districts face hardship due to multiple years of declining enrollment. Housing SB 1566 — Making Affordable Housing Pencil: I brought SB 1566 to the Labor and Business committee at the beginning of the session after hearing that affordable housing projects were stalling out or being shelved all together because of the way a rule was being interpreted and implemented by BOLI. This bill was an effort to reduce construction cost for affordable housing projects and was met with swift opposition from Labor Unions, however public support for this bill was robust. This bill would have cut red tape, making it less expensive to build homes that lower-income Oregonians can afford- instead this bill died in committee, proving the power of the Big Labor Unions. We are glad to hear there is talks ongoing with Oregon Housing and BOLI to get better clarification on prevailing wage for affordable housing. HB 4120 — Residential Tenancy: Allows landlords to ban smoking in residential tenancies, giving property owners a new tool to protect buildings and other tenants. HB 4035 — Urban Growth Boundary Fixes: Technical fixes to SB 1537 (2024) streamlines the Urban Growth Boundary (UGB) expansion process: Removed the "severely rent-burdened" threshold cities must display to trigger the land use expansion process. Cities must not have large undeveloped internal tracts (20+ net residential acres) to qualify. Resource lands may be used when they make up 80% of land surrounding the UGB within a quarter mile. Cities over 25,000 population may expand by up to 150 net residential acres (increased from 100 acres under SB 1537). HB 4082 — One-time UGB Expansion for Seniors: Allows cities of 25,000 or more to bring in up to 100 acres, and smaller cities up to 50 acres, for a one-time UGB expansion. This tool is restricted to housing that benefits people aged 55 and older. HB 4037 — Housing Omnibus: A broad package of housing reforms including: City and County Housing Project Funding: Technical fixes to the Moderate-Income Revolving Loan Program to make homeownership development more feasible. CDFI Predevelopment Loans: Expands project eligibility and funding amounts under the Moderate-Income Housing Predevelopment Loan Program. Housing Enforcement: Fixes a technical error that had limited enforcement orders to cities above 10,000 population. Building Plan Self-Certification: Expands to engineered and non-prescriptive building plans. Housing Application Review: Requires applications meeting clear and objective standards to be processed without an initial public hearing; limits land use appeals to the applicant. Disaster Tenancy Protections: Creates standards for tenant access, obligations, and rights to rented units after a natural disaster. Surplus State Land for Housing: Clarifies priority order for acquiring surplus state lands for affordable and market-rate housing development. SB 1561 — Natural Disaster Rebuilding: Makes it easier to rebuild a home after a natural disaster. This is a significant bill as there was groups looking to not allow home owners to rebuild after their house was destroyed in rural parts of Oregon. Public Safety HB 4145 —Measure 114 Delay: Pushes back the implementation of Measure 114 to January 1, 2028, while the Oregon Supreme Court completes its ruling on the case. This turned into a good gun bill from a bad one. There were a number of "anti police" bills that passed on partisan lines. I am very concerned about ongoing erosion of respect for law enforcement in our country. We must have order to be a nation, our police are tasked with keeping things in order on both the local and national level. We have laws, they enforce them. There is a process and it just feels like the majority party just wants to use our police as political pawns, I don't like it. Taxes & Fiscal Policy HB 4125 & SJR 201 (DEFEATED)—Protecting the Kicker: Both bills that would have modified Oregon's kicker tax rebate were successfully killed, protecting taxpayers' rebates. SB 1511 — Estate Tax (DEFEATED): The defeat of Senate Bill 1511 is a win for Oregon Taxpayers, while the bill raised the exemption threshold, it simultaneously imposed some of the highest estate tax rates in the nation topping out at nearly 20%. This bill would have severe repercussions for successful small business owners, farmers, and entrepreneurs that would have faced an even steeper tax burden at death. Oregon already struggles to retain high net worth residents and imposing near record tax rates would only accelerate that exodus, ultimately costing the state income tax revenue, jobs and investment. By defeating this bill the legislature has the opportunity to go back to the drawing board and pursue estate tax reform that truly protects Oregon families, keeps generational businesses intact, and makes the state a more attractive place to live, work and build a legacy. SB 1507 — Federal Tax Disconnect: Raises taxes by approximately $300 million while offering an extremely limited $25 million tax credit in return. This bill remains a significant concern for Oregon businesses and families. HB 4098 (DEFEATED) —Insurance Cost Protection: Would have raised insurance prices, was successfully killed for another year — continuing a decade-long effort to protect Oregonians from higher insurance costs. Economic Development HB 4084 — Governor's Prosperity Bill, designed to boost Oregon's economic competitiveness: Fast-track permitting in limited circumstances Funding for industrial site readiness Enterprise zone program improvements One-year moratorium on using enterprise zones for data centers SB 1586 — from Senator Sollman, (DID NOT PASS). It would have brought 1,700 acres into Hillsboro's UGB for advanced manufacturing and semiconductor development, expanded Oregon's R&D tax credit, created an optional local property tax waiver for new machinery and equipment in advanced manufacturing. SB 1501 — Legislation related to the Moda Center and the Portland Trail Blazers organization passed this session. Details to follow as implementation proceeds. Recreation & Liability HB 1517 — Generally makes liability waivers enforceable for recreational activities. However, the bill contains several exemptions that limit how much it can reduce costs for recreation businesses and operators. Campaign Finance HB 4018 — Makes important technical fixes to Oregon's recently adopted campaign finance law. Contribution limits for state legislative campaigns take effect January 1, 2027. I am for new campaign finance legislation, however I also think we need an overhaul on our systems and the best way to curb corruption is to put term limits on legislators in effect. Transportation SB 1599 — Gas tax measure: Moves the gas tax ballot measure election to the May election cycle. District 5 continues to be full of community energy! A major milestone worth celebrating in southern Lincoln County was the official grand opening and ribbon-cutting for the new Yachats Public Library, a modern, expanded facility that replaced the original 1973 structure. The new library features increased space for books and community resources, a larger children’s area, public computers, and a community room — marking a significant investment in lifelong learning and community gathering in Yachats. Looking ahead, there are several upcoming opportunities for engagement and community participation across the district. The Oregon Coast Council for the Arts in Newport has planned spring and early summer performances and exhibitions, while the calendar of events in Yachats includes arts and crafts fairs, cultural gatherings, and recreational activities that highlight the unique coastal character of our communities. These events reflect the rich cultural and civic life of District 5 — from library celebrations and festivals to arts, learning, and community gatherings. I am grateful to be a part of such a vibrant community. The connection between people and their governmen t is bolstered when the public has substantial opportunity to let their concerns be heard by their elected officials. subject: We need to reach 1 million patriots calling for term limits
body:
You know it and I know it -- Congress is broken.

| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zftene5fq36dlb81iq15g3i9oggac411a99d3710_rp22sh2s8i6epr6ctjmcp34cth2bs)
---
| | Dear Fellow Conservative,You know it and I know it -- Congress is broken. Politicians have turned “serving the people” into “serving themselves.” They use their positions to get richer and richer every year, while you and I get left behind.Left-wing radicals like Ilhan Omar, Rashida Tlaib, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez work to destroy our country from within. And Washington never fixes anything. **[Today, WE THE PEOPLE have a chance to do something about it when you sign your “Time for Term Limits” petition and submit it in the next 72 hours.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z2jdco5petnmceetrlcu07s1eicd5s4snmcjvjuo_rp22sh2s8i6epr6ctjmcp34cth2bs)** Our Founding Fathers never intended for government service to be a permanent career. George Washington famously served just two terms — then went home.Our Founding Fathers also said our government was made for a “moral and religious people.” And they understood that if that moral compass broke down, Congress could easily steer America in the wrong direction, become a do-nothing body, or make government a gravy train for themselves.That’s why they included a powerful safeguard in our Constitution -- an escape hatch -- enshrined in Article V. If Congress ever became too corrupt to fix itself, Article V. says the states can use this provision in the Constitution to act.34 state legislatures can call a convention, propose term limits -- and Congress can’t do a thing about it. [**Here at AMAC Action, we have led the term limits movement in the past, and we are ready to put our efforts behind the movement once again.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z21rcc5bd62dqj7p8f4es2h31ukivlu45chc4uu8_rp22sh2s8i6epr6ctjmcp34cth2bs)
---
[ **Time for Term Limits** ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z29ujcq337fb8p26fc9rs9k68tsibl17380bgv0g_rp22sh2s8i6epr6ctjmcp34cth2bs)
---
My friend, can you imagine Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez spending 30 more years in Congress?? We are AMAC Action. “AMAC” stands for Association of Mature American Citizens. And when it comes to standing up for the rights of Americans, “action” is what we’re known for.President Trump has said that AMAC Action is so effective that members of Congress run the other way when they see our delegates coming down the hall. And our **“Time for Term Limits”** Petition Drive certainly has Washington lifers on the run![**Please sign your petition and submit it in the next 72 hours.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z80183eesqin3m94m1h2jaj8vbvo72526ajjbm98_rp22sh2s8i6epr6ctjmcp34cth2bs)
---
**>>** No more golden pensions for people who work 170 days a year and spend half of that just trying to get reelected.**>>** No more using the power of the office to destroy American values from within.**>>** No more insider deals to get rich.**>>** No more jobs for life with nothing to show for it!
---
Some of these grifters and America-haters have been “working” in Congress over 30, and even 40 years!
---
* **Maxine Waters — 34 years**
* **Chuck Schumer — 44 years**
* **Patty Murray — 33 years**

---
They’ve been in the swamp so long they’ve grown gills. Please – let’s not let them drag America down into the swamp with them. It’s time to use the escape hatch our Founders left for us.34 state legislatures are needed. What will embolden states to act is seeing a massive groundswell of support for term limits from millions of Americans just like you.That’s why AMAC Action is spearheading this massive 50-state Petition Drive and why you got my email today.You’ve proven that you’re a patriot who can be counted on to take action. **[Please sign your “Time for Term Limits” petition and submit it in the next 72 hours with your sacrificial donation of $35, $50 or more to spread this national campaign across America.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z0h6p2i1gf733no7a68n820snstq3kf6929ffdto_rp22sh2s8i6epr6ctjmcp34cth2bs)** We need to reach **1 million** patriots with petitions just like yours.And that takes time and money.The Washington lifers are counting on having more power, influence, and resources than the American people.They’re counting on our complacency and despair.But here at AMAC Action we say: Let’s finish the fight our Founders began and restore America’s government to the people.Your $35 gift is enough to send and collect 50 more **“Time for Term Limits”** petitions across email, text, and mail. Your gift of $70 funds 100 more **“Time for Term Limits”** petitions.Singlehandedly, you are an indispensable force-multiplier in this effort. But if you do nothing, nothing changes.
---
* Immigration policy will never get fixed and just stay a meaningless election year talking point.
* America’s spending and debt will continue to grow unchecked. Remember when we had a balanced budget? We can get back there if career politicians do something!
* Social Security will keep getting raided while real policies to protect your benefits sit on the back burner.
* Healthcare costs will do nothing but skyrocket leaving seniors vulnerable.
* America’s children will stay trapped in the leftwing indoctrination centers we call “public schools.”
* Radicals like Ilhan Omar, Corey Booker, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez will continue to undermine America’s founding values.
* And the Washington, D.C. fat-cats will just get fatter and lazier.

---
Please join our army of patriots who are fed-up with the Washington lifers who work against our interests while our country sinks. What’s even more frustrating is that President Trump has policies that can save the ship and Washington lifers stand in his way! **[Your signed “Time for Term Limits” petition is critical. And we appreciate your donation whether it’s $35, $50 or anything higher or lower. What’s most important is that you respond in the next 72 hours.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zebbm8gdvatq2juq9vojvkugk1pu99u7sv3q7g00_rp22sh2s8i6epr6ctjmcp34cth2bs)** **One million “Time for Term Limits” petitions is a bold goal but we can do it if we all pitch in.** Every dollar helps. Every signature counts. Every day matters.Thank you and may God bless you and these United States.
---
| | With hope and urgency,
---
**Rebecca Weber,_Chairwoman_****AMAC Action**

body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Bolts: Ohio Bans Grace Periods for Mail Ballots, Fulfilling Trump’s Wishes [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=031726_1&amount=25]
Ohio just made it harder to vote by mail, Team .
Senate Bill 293, which was recently signed into law, repeals Ohio’s practice of counting mail ballots that are postmarked prior to Election Day but that arrive up to four days after polls close. Now, any ballots delayed in the mail that arrive after Election Day won't count in Ohio.
This follows executive orders from President Trump, who is against mail-in voting despite voting that way himself , and has called for ending these so-called grace periods for mail ballots everywhere. Ohio’s new law follows his lead, threatening thousands of votes in the process.
We've said it before and we'll keep saying it: Mail-in balloting is safe and secure. It's a nonpartisan way for eligible voters to make their voices heard in our elections. And now it's harder for them to participate in elections in Ohio, whether they're a military member voting from overseas, someone who is immunocompromised, in a nursing home, or any other reason for voting by mail.
Defending vote-by-mail is a crucial part of protecting our fundamental right to vote. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to support mail-in voting across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=031726_1&amount=35]

subject: Re: Urgent: Speak out to stop plans to clearcut Western Oregon forests!
body:
Hi Peter,
I want to make sure you saw this: the Trump administration is considering a plan that would dramatically increase logging on 2.5 million acres of old-growth forests across western Oregon . These are the very forests that we know and love.

Peter,
Oregon’s forests are under threat — and your voice is needed right now.
The Trump administration has announced plans to revise management of 2.5 million acres of public forests across western Oregon in order to dramatically increase logging levels.
If implemented, this proposal could open the door to widespread clearcutting across some of the most biologically rich forests in the Pacific Northwest. These forests provide habitat for species like coho salmon, marbled murrelets, and northern spotted owls, while also protecting clean drinking water, supporting recreation, and helping communities adapt to climate change.
The plan could:
* Return logging levels to those not seen since the 1960s
* Shrink protections for rivers and streams
* Reduce safeguards for mature and old-growth forests
* Prioritize timber production over wildlife, recreation, and clean water
Places many Oregonians know and love, including areas near the Molalla River, Marys Peak, Alsea Falls, and the Rogue River, could be impacted.
Right now, federal officials are accepting public comments on this proposal. This is one of the most important opportunities we have to push back.

name: Barlow For Wyo
subject: Barlow For Wyoming Newsletter
body:
Hard Work and Luck
| | | | | | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KKY5VFW2YDVA0DKQB0DAEYGD_0)
---
| **Welcome to the Barlow for Wyoming Newsletter. Your hub for latest news, information and upcoming events.**
---
|
---
| | |
---
| Hard Work and Luck
---
| Hi friends,
Happy St. Patrick's Day! There's a quote often attributed to Thomas Jefferson that says, "I am a great believer in luck; I find the harder I work, the more luck I have." Showing up and doing the work has consistently yielded better results in my life as well, and I plan to continue that work for Wyoming. I feel lucky and blessed by the show of support from all of you who are subscribed here, who follow our social media, and who are supporting our efforts in multiple ways. I see it, and I am grateful. Please share this newsletter and continue to help our Wyoming neighbors connect to the campaign. As we head into the busiest months of the Barlow for Governor effort, I am prepared to work harder than ever, traveling to communities to hear what's important to citizens and sharing our platform across the state. Keep an eye on our pinned campaign schedule here and on Facebook, which is updated with new events every week. We anticipate being in all 23 counties again! We will attend the Wyoming State Parks Conference in Sheridan this week before heading to the SW part of the state for events in Star Valley, Alpine, Pinedale, and Kemmerer. Looking forward to being back on the trail, \- Eric
---
|
---
| | | SF101 Veto Override Vote The legislature met for its final day of the 2026 Budget Session last week, and one of our final duties was to consider overriding the Governor's vetoes, including SF 101, the Second Amendment Protection Act (SAPA). I strongly support the Second Amendment and have a long record defending those rights. I also believe our laws should not unintentionally create roadblocks that make it harder to keep our communities safe. After reviewing the bill and spending time visiting with Campbell County Sheriff Scott Matheny and other County Sheriffs from around the state, as well as other Wyoming law enforcement professionals, I voted against overriding the Governor’s Veto of SF101. Before making this decision, I also spent time reviewing the Governor’s veto letter and supporting documentation from federal law enforcement partners. I remain committed to protecting constitutional rights while also making sure Wyoming law enforcement has the tools they need to do their work.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | IN THE NEWS
[WyoFile - LTE](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KKY5VFW2YDVA0DKQB0DAEYGD_1) "Thank you, Sen. Barlow, members of the Wyoming Legislature, and Gov. Gordon for listening to the input from the thousands of people in our state who recognize the importance of these lands and the weight of this moment. This session's momentous turn of events is an achievement worth celebrating and will go a long way toward maintaining Wyoming's outdoor heritage and economy for generations to come." \- Ellen and Steve Bechtel, Lander
---
| | |
---
|
---

CAN YOU HELP WITH THE NEXT ORDER??
You've all been patient, and FINALLY, the Barlow for Governor signs are starting to appear across the Wyoming landscape, with strong backing for the Wyoming wind and weather! Many of you have asked for smaller yard signs, which will arrive for distribution this spring.
But, as you know...we have A LOT of land to cover. Can you help with an additional donation to keep the sign printer moving? Click the link below!

| Peter,
Democratic Congressman Jared Golden (D-ME) just ended his reelection campaign because of threats to his family.
Citing his experience of spending last thanksgiving in hiding and the escalating wave of political violence and assassinations, Golden announced that he will be retiring from Congress at the end of his term.
This changes everything, his district, Maine's 2nd Congressional District, is the most vulnerable blue district in the US. Trump won here by 9 points in 2024.

We are now outnumbered, outgunned, and are being circled by the vultures. Already MAGA is throwing everything behind my extreme far-right opponent "Trump before there was Trump" Former Maine Gov. Paul LePage.

### Gender Ideology: One Mother’s Story
---

| | January Littlejohn joins the program to discuss the latest developments in the national debate over gender medicine, parental rights, and medical treatments for minors. Her advocacy began after her own family’s experience, when her teenage daughter began questioning her gender identity — a moment that propelled her into becoming a leading voice for parents navigating similar challenges. Today, she serves as a Senior Fellow and Parent Advocate at Do No Harm, where she promotes evidence-based medicine and advocates for policies aimed at protecting minors from medical harm. | | If you watch the news, you’d think American women are on the brink of collapse. The loudest voices online are pushing a swirl of exaggerated — and often untrue — claims. We’re told women no longer need men or children. Some even suggest that women in other countries enjoy freedoms that American women are too “oppressed” to experience. And we’re told, bizarrely, that transgender issues are simply women’s issues in disguise. These ideas — and the emotional spiral they create — have left many left-leaning women feeling frantic, victimized, and ready to record another viral video rant. But the noise doesn’t reflect reality. Read the full blog by joining our free membership at Moms TownSquare.

subject: Spineless Lindsey Graham
body:
|
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127503308/608279030/-639635826?refcode=WUEFHO33_20260317_AndrewsSplit_ALL_v1s3&sourceid=1058051&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0Y2ZkOWI5OC0xODIyLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zY-AVZ3j29vwAJwdLj8etJ3RVjmOFvzDV5Q5qba2Pm0=) I’m Dr. Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, a mom of three, and the Democrat running for U.S. Senate to defeat Republican Lindsey Graham in South Carolina.

If we flip this seat, we can end Lindsey Graham’s career and help Democrats retake the Senate, and expand the map for Democrats in future elections.

I know this won’t be easy. But I’ve treated kids who were shot, hospitalized, and failed by broken systems. Nothing about this moment feels optional. ****[**We need an overwhelming surge of grassroots support to prove that we can finally defeat Lindsey Graham. So I’m humbly asking: Will you chip in a split donation of $50, $25, or even a $3 donation between EMILYs List and my campaign right now so we can hit our fundraising goals? >>**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127503309/608279031/-639635826?refcode=WUEFHO33_20260317_AndrewsSplit_ALL_v1s3&sourceid=1058051&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0Y2ZkOWI5OC0xODIyLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zY-AVZ3j29vwAJwdLj8etJ3RVjmOFvzDV5Q5qba2Pm0=)****

Let me introduce myself.

I’ve spent nearly 20 years serving my community as a pediatrician, treating everything from asthma and violent trauma to the emotional toll of growing up in poverty.

I’ve seen what bad policy does to good families — and I’ve seen kids suffer because people like Lindsey Graham would rather protect their own power than protect children.

In 2022, after 15 years of working in hospitals, I ran for Congress because I knew our kids needed a voice in Washington. I lost — and I told my oldest daughter I wouldn’t run again.

But then Trump’s chaos came back.

And Lindsey Graham? He cheered.

The truth is, I’m scared. And I’m angry. And I’m done waiting.

So I’m stepping up — because our kids, and this country can’t afford another six years of Lindsey Graham. ****[**I’m building a people-powered campaign to flip South Carolina and give kids the voice they deserve. clean_body: | = I’m Dr. Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, a mom of three, and the Democrat running for U.S. Senate to defeat Republican Lindsey Graham in South Carolina. If we flip this seat, we can end Lindsey Graham’s career and help Democrats retake the Senate, and expand the map for Democrats in future elections. I know this won’t be easy. But I’ve treated kids who were shot, hospitalized, and failed by broken systems. Nothing about this moment feels optional. **= Let me introduce myself. I’ve spent nearly 20 years serving my community as a pediatrician, treating everything from asthma and violent trauma to the emotional toll of growing up in poverty. I’ve seen what bad policy does to good families — and I’ve seen kids suffer because people like Lindsey Graham would rather protect their own power than protect children. In 2022, after 15 years of working in hospitals, I ran for Congress because I knew our kids needed a voice in Washington. I lost — and I told my oldest daughter I wouldn’t run again. But then Trump’s chaos came back. And Lindsey Graham? He cheered. The truth is, I’m scared. And I’m angry. And I’m done waiting. So I’m stepping up — because our kids, and this country can’t afford another six years of Lindsey Graham. =** If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thank you — from the bottom of my heart. body:
**Friend,**
I need to tell you something that made my blood boil.
Students at Cerritos College set up a tent in the **free speech square** — the place literally designated for open conversation — and invited anyone to come debate them on socialism, communism, and immigration.
The school told them to shut it down. Called it _"disturbing the peace."_
Disturbing the peace? For having a conversation? For asking people to _prove me wrong_?
I have heard those words before. Not on a college campus — on a fishing boat in the South China Sea.
My father whispered them in 1985 as he hid my family under a tarp with nothing but the clothes on our backs. He was betting our lives that somewhere on the other side of that ocean, people were **free to speak.**
Three days on that boat. My mother holding us so tight I could feel her heartbeat. Not knowing if we would be found by pirates or rescued. Not knowing if we would live.
We survived. Thirty months in refugee camps. And in 1987, we stepped onto American soil with $20 in my father's pocket and tears on his face — because he made it. He got his family to the one place on earth where you could stand in a public square and say what you believe.
Now I am watching students be punished for doing **exactly that.**
### This Is Personal
My father did not cross an ocean so that American students could be silenced for having conversations. He did not spend three days praying in the dark of a fishing boat so that a school administrator could call free speech "disturbing the peace."
**I will not sit quietly and watch it happen. Not while I am breathing.**
This is not about left or right. This is about whether we still believe in the thing that makes America _America._
The right to speak. The right to disagree. The right to stand in a square and say: _prove me wrong._
That right is what my father risked everything for. And I will fight for it every single day — in Congress, on campuses, in every room where someone tries to tell a free person to sit down and be quiet.
**But I cannot do it alone.**

clean_body: Friend, I need to tell you something that made my blood boil. Students at Cerritos College set up a tent in the free speech square — the place literally designated for open conversation — and invited anyone to come debate them on socialism, communism, and immigration. The school told them to shut it down. Called it "disturbing the peace." Disturbing the peace? For having a conversation? For asking people to prove me wrong? I have heard those words before. Not on a college campus — on a fishing boat in the South China Sea. My father whispered them in 1985 as he hid my family under a tarp with nothing but the clothes on our backs. He was betting our lives that somewhere on the other side of that ocean, people were free to speak. Three days on that boat. My mother holding us so tight I could feel her heartbeat. Not knowing if we would be found by pirates or rescued. Not knowing if we would live. We survived. Thirty months in refugee camps. And in 1987, we stepped onto American soil with $20 in my father's pocket and tears on his face — because he made it. He got his family to the one place on earth where you could stand in a public square and say what you believe. Now I am watching students be punished for doing exactly that. This Is Personal My father did not cross an ocean so that American students could be silenced for having conversations. He did not spend three days praying in the dark of a fishing boat so that a school administrator could call free speech "disturbing the peace." I will not sit quietly and watch it happen. Not while I am breathing. This is not about left or right. This is about whether we still believe in the thing that makes America America. The right to speak. The right to disagree. The right to stand in a square and say: prove me wrong. That right is what my father risked everything for. And I will fight for it every single day — in Congress, on campuses, in every room where someone tries to tell a free person to sit down and be quiet. But I cannot do it alone. My father arrived with $20. That was everything. It was enough to start a new life in a free country. Today, your $20 says something just as powerful: we do not silence people in America. Not on my watch. Folks,
**Believe it or not, Election Day is three weeks from today.** That’s why we want to make sure you have everything you need to vote.
Below is a quick guide with the most important resources and deadlines.
* * *
**_How do I register to vote?_** ☑️
You can register to vote online by **[clicking here](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/282?t=3&akid=1249%2E294397%2EwDf1Bn)**. _The deadline to register online is tomorrow,_ so don’t wait!
If you prefer to register to vote in person, you can do so at your municipal clerk’s office until April 3 at 5 p.m, or you can register on Election Day at your polling location. Speaking of...
* * *
**_Where do I vote in person?_** 📍
You can find your polling location by **[clicking here](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/287?t=4&akid=1249%2E294397%2EwDf1Bn)**.
* * *
**_When can I vote?_**
If you requested an absentee ballot, you can track its status by **[clicking here](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/288?t=5&akid=1249%2E294397%2EwDf1Bn)**.
Early, in-person voting starts around March 24 through early April (hours vary by municipality).
**Election Day is on April 7.**
* * *
Finally, if you want to check what’s on your ballot, contact your municipal clerk, or find other information, visit **[MyVote Wisconsin’s website](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/289?t=6&akid=1249%2E294397%2EwDf1Bn)**.
**If you have friends or family who may find this guide helpful, forward them this email.** Thanks so much for making a plan to vote!
Forward,
Team Taylor

_Hoppers_ , Pixar's latest feature film, opens with a flashback. Mabel, who will grow up to be our teenage protagonist--a skateboard-riding environmentalist staging one-woman protests in defense of local wildlife--is just a child, staring at her classroom terrarium, home to a much-poked and prodded turtle. She waits until the recess bell rings and her classmates sprint outside before pulling the turtle out of the tank and stowing it carefully in her backpack. Soon, she's cramming the backpack with every critter in the building--a guinea pig, birds, mice, a snake--and making a run for freedom. But the heist comes to an ignominious end when Mabel is intercepted, and we see on her face--as she's reprimanded by teachers and parents--a deep sense of anger and sadness, not just that her jailbreak was foiled, but that she's the only one who sees the need for a jailbreak at all. Why don't any of her classmates, her teachers, or her parents give a damn?
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9hYXJvbnJlZ3VuYmVyZy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE5MTI1MjY2NywicyI6NDk4MTE3MCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc3Mzc2NTM0OSwiZXhwIjoyMDg5MzQxMzQ5LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.nlYBewyjjJlXGu-Y_Eki2kXutd6oR5Ovfs2IuoPD0O0?)
The lonesomeness of Mabel's fight for animals remains a central theme in _Hoppers_. We see it again immediately upon cutting to the present day, when Mabel stands alone in front of a demolition crew, trying to stop the bulldozing of a wooded glade--her childhood haven--that the town mayor, Jerry, wants to turn into a new expressway, "getting you where you need to go up to four minutes faster." Mayor Jerry tells Mabel that she's the only one who wants to save the glade, whereas everyone in town wants the highway. To prove him wrong, Mabel launches a petition drive, which leads to a montage of doors getting slammed in her face--once more, it seems like Mabel is the only one who cares.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/955cf5f4-904c-4bf2-8d44-73d9e22ef0a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
After that, the story becomes increasingly zany, as Mabel discovers an experimental "hopper" technology that allows her to Avatar herself into a lifelike beaver robot and set off on a journey to recruit real beavers to return to the glade (since beavers can bring back the wetlands that might create a permitting obstacle to Mayor Jerry's overpass plans--because yes, this Pixar movie has a distinctly anti-abundance bro sensibility).
But throughout these madcap adventures, the film reiterates that taking the plight of non-human animals seriously can be a lonely endeavor. In one moment of despair, Mabel turns to a beaver she has befriended, and cries, "Why doesn't anyone else _care_?"
Watching this movie with my five-year-old son beside me was a peculiar emotional experience. He is a committed vegetarian, and sometimes--particularly when he sees people he loves, like his cousins or grandparents, eating meat--he'll get sad or frustrated, unable to wrap his head around how people he knows to be good could appear so unconcerned about the suffering of other living creatures. But for the most part, he still lives in a world where feeling empathy and compassion for non-humans is the norm.
It's almost a universal truth that kids love animals, and this fondness is generally encouraged. Until, at some point, it's not; at some point, we become adults, and adults are supposed to put aside childish preoccupations with animals and center our worldview on people. Understanding humans as the only beings whose welfare truly matters is practically a marker of one's maturity. And to resist this dominant perspective is to invite ridicule.
Anyone who's spent time as a vegetarian or vegan knows a bit about that ridicule. The internet is full of [articles with headlines](https://substack.com/redirect/a45063e0-d7e8-43ca-9612-93b6902ea3a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) like "[Why do people hate vegans so much?](https://substack.com/redirect/55c4f446-3474-4e05-bd91-99859bedd131?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" This animus isn't just anecdotal--a peer-reviewed [study](https://substack.com/redirect/67f1d55d-f9a0-4a1a-be9d-914ad104dcff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from 2015 found that omnivores evaluated vegetarians and vegans more negatively than people with other dietary restrictions, with those motivated by animal rights or environmental concerns treated particularly poorly. And new versions of this scorn are regularly evolving, with perhaps the most recent iteration coming from the billionaire funders and millionaire pundits behind the abundance movement, who have endeavored to [reframe](https://substack.com/redirect/e77dfb81-aede-4959-9d46-9b2cfecf7d36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [environmentalists](https://substack.com/redirect/e0d5b163-500d-427a-8f00-d8eca2c8b3f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--not oligarchs or fascists, but rather people like Mabel fighting to protect their local glades from expressways--as the [source of all society's ills](https://substack.com/redirect/5d1b4c26-c719-4b4b-a206-19fc6c5c8b21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/731e99f1-89cf-4197-9240-65f2dbba1c39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Just sharing this headline, from the abundance bros at the fossil fuel-backed Breakthrough Institute, to show I'm not exaggerating here.
Of course, there have been valid reasons to criticize the environmental movement over the years, not least the [white supremacy](https://substack.com/redirect/06b127d2-dc2b-4a0c-bf52-af8d4c52d8ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of a number of its early founders. And given that our world is overflowing with more human suffering than any one mind could ever hope to get a grip on, it's a completely reasonable choice to limit one's empathic focus to our species.
But that doesn't explain why people so frequently treat the destruction of nature and the suffering of animals as undeserving of legitimate concern. If misery and loss are bad, then these are among the greatest catastrophes taking place today. Around 10 billion chickens, turkeys, cows, and pigs are [slaughtered](https://substack.com/redirect/3575639e-5dc8-42cd-8a70-968be8970302?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the U.S. every year. Animals that research suggests are [just as smart](https://substack.com/redirect/8e58f239-e1c7-4a28-9a36-59ae78ba7230?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as the dogs and cats we adore, and just as capable of joy and affection and sadness and suffering, are subjected to the most cruel, barbaric, would-get-you-immediately-arrested-for-animal-abuse conditions that you can possibly imagine (though I suspect many of us are literally not capable of imagining the actual horrors of this factory farmed existence).
Meanwhile, we are rapidly turning the rest of our planet--to our current knowledge the most uniquely precious place in the entire universe--into a degraded wasteland. The statistics can feel somewhat numbing. Humanity has caused the loss of [85 percent](https://substack.com/redirect/b559aa95-0a2f-401f-b515-b241d1412207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of all wild mammals and [half](https://substack.com/redirect/eda32746-e015-441d-bd2c-3d8a423458d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of all plants. Since 1970, North America's wild bird population has [fallen](https://substack.com/redirect/ddae60c5-c89a-4fa4-9c43-dfb3f2054dfc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by three billion. In that same time, [human activities have](https://substack.com/redirect/12ea0508-f08c-4bc3-9935-de94bc8c981b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) significantly altered 75 percent of the ice-free land surface on the planet, and destroyed over 85 percent of the world's wetlands. When I watch _Planet Earth_ or other nature documentaries with my son, he is shown a world teeming with wildlife. But in reality, the beautiful diversity of animals these shows depict are marginalized exceptions to what our planet has become. Humans and our miserable livestock now [account](https://substack.com/redirect/78728bc8-642c-4440-aed6-2739ef22c415?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for more than 96 percent of all mammal biomass on Earth. Every other mammal--every whale, big cat, moose, beaver, monkey, kangaroo, mouse, elephant, deer, fox, all of them--in combination adds up to just four percent.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/baf898b1-eb1d-4cf7-918b-e1afce5d2a56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Indeed, we are in the midst of the [sixth mass extinction](https://substack.com/redirect/e2d25668-d837-43a8-a0e2-ac51e87e8082?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Earth's history. Every single day, species that have been evolving and adapting and surviving for millions or tens of millions or in some cases hundreds of millions of years are being brought to an abrupt and inescapably [permanent end](https://substack.com/redirect/d65b9932-0815-460b-a39d-035c6a3b61b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--life forms that will never again be seen in the universe, because of us. My son, who loves dinosaurs as much as he loves all other animals, will sometimes get sad thinking about the asteroid that caused the fifth mass extinction event 66 million years ago. This was the single most catastrophic moment in our planet's history from a biological perspective--every non-avian dinosaur lineage wiped out, and countless other species too, so that for millions of years [afterwards](https://substack.com/redirect/b96780df-19d6-4669-b6ac-cf61b165d770?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Earth was a barren world of small and monotonously similar creatures. I'm still never quite sure how to communicate to my son that we are creating, of our own free will, a comparable disaster today.
And yet, this almost incomprehensible tragedy is barely discussed--even by people like me. There's no crisis in the world that causes me as much existential anguish as this one, and yet I barely ever speak about it, post about it, write about it. I write about climate change, but climate--while it's a major cause of biodiversity loss--is a fundamentally human story; it's our civilization that is at risk of collapsing due to climate change, which has driven nearly every [civilizational collapse](https://substack.com/redirect/acc9f508-af86-442d-8b5c-4af760df7596?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in human history. The breakdown of global ecological systems and the mass suffering of animals are less human-centered problems, which is why it almost feels embarrassing to take these desperately urgent crises seriously. In most contexts, doing so is a lonely affair.
So it's pretty remarkable that _Hoppers_ --a movie about a young woman who takes the natural world as seriously as it deserves to be taken, while grappling with the heartache and fury she feels towards everyone around her who couldn't care less--has been for two weekends in a row the [top film](https://substack.com/redirect/171c96c2-d270-415b-96f5-57a0e8345138?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) virtually everywhere on the planet, with a global box office take of $165 million so far. That's a lot of people who have watched and enjoyed this story, and--perhaps, to some small degree--internalized some of its themes. In a moment when good news can feel hard to come by, that feels worth celebrating.
When we got home from our screening, my wife, who hadn't joined us at the theater, asked our son what the movie was about. He said it was about "believing." A bit of a head-scratcher, that answer--there's not really any explicit discussion of believing in _Hoppers_ ; no scenes where Tinkerbell is brought back to life through the power of belief. And I couldn't get the kid to expand on his initial response, which was open-ended enough to allow an essay-writer to layer all sorts of profound meanings on top. He's five--five-year-olds say weird things all the time.
But I can't help but give his response my own spin. After watching this movie, and seeing the world's response to it, what I am choosing to believe is that there are a lot of us who care about the non-human world. If we all just had the courage to be as loud and proud about that belief as Mabel, maybe this fight wouldn't have to be so lonely.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3e98b3b3-97b0-4593-8ace-5dc4fcea5453?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This essay appeared in _[The New Republic](https://substack.com/redirect/37778142-c7bb-4938-9d70-ce524163c84c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_. Thanks so much for reading, it means the world to me!

Mabel, who will grow up to be our teenage protagonist--a skateboard-riding environmentalist staging one-woman protests in defense of local wildlife--is just a child, staring at her classroom terrarium, home to a much-poked and prodded turtle. Soon, she's cramming the backpack with every critter in the building--a guinea pig, birds, mice, a snake--and making a run for freedom. But the heist comes to an ignominious end when Mabel is intercepted, and we see on her face--as she's reprimanded by teachers and parents--a deep sense of anger and sadness, not just that her jailbreak was foiled, but that she's the only one who sees the need for a jailbreak at all. Why don't any of her classmates, her teachers, or her parents give a damn? ? The lonesomeness of Mabel's fight for animals remains a central theme in Hoppers. We see it again immediately upon cutting to the present day, when Mabel stands alone in front of a demolition crew, trying to stop the bulldozing of a wooded glade--her childhood haven--that the town mayor, Jerry, wants to turn into a new expressway, "getting you where you need to go up to four minutes faster." Mayor Jerry tells Mabel that she's the only one who wants to save the glade, whereas everyone in town wants the highway. body:
** The 2026 Autism Health Summit is Almost Here!
------------------------------------------------------------
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JyPTtXfKYd8&mc_cid=f4f3dce82d&mc_eid=UNIQID

April 24–26, 2026 | Legacy Center Resort & Spa | San Diego, California

The Autism Health Summit is just 5 weeks away, and we are excited to welcome our community for three powerful days of education, connection, and collaboration. As our flagship educational event, the Summit brings together leading voices in research, medicine, advocacy, and integrative health. This annual gathering is designed for parents, practitioners, researchers, and advocates seeking deeper insight into autism and neurological health from a whole-body, whole-family perspective.

We are honored to host an extraordinary lineup of speakers, including Aaron Siri, Del Bigtree, Dr. Toby Rogers, Dr. Sabine Hazan, Dr. Dayan Goodenowe, Ed Clay, and many more respected experts and thought leaders. Together, they will explore emerging research, clinical insights, environmental factors, and practical strategies that families and professionals can apply in real life. To view the full list of speakers and sessions, click HERE to see our agenda (https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/ahsconference.com%2Fagenda%2F/b43o/ShTEAQ/AQ/4d02b33e-7454-44ba-b7b7-0f0a3eb4ae6e/2/pf1jVdRQuC?mc_cid=f4f3dce82d&mc_eid=UNIQID) .

In partnership with Cellular Performance Institute (CPI), updated findings from their CPI funded clinical trial for autism will be presented at the Autism Health Summit.

The Summit will take place at the beautiful Legacy Center Resort & Spa in San Diego, where attendees can book a room at a special group rate of $199 per night. To reserve your room, please use the conference room block link HERE (https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/be.synxis.com%2F%3Fadult%3D1%26arrive%3D2026-04-22%26chain%3D27003%26child%3D0%26config%3DGRPCONFIG%26currency%3DUSD%26depart%3D2026-04-27%26group%3DAUTISM26%26hotel%3D31076%26level%3Dhotel%26locale%3Den-US%26productcurrency%3DUSD%26rooms%3D1%26theme%3DGRPTHEME/b43o/ShTEAQ/AQ/4d02b33e-7454-44ba-b7b7-0f0a3eb4ae6e/3/sOOkN_Cd1M?mc_cid=f4f3dce82d&mc_eid=UNIQID) or call (619) 782-9155 and use block code Autism26.

To celebrate the final countdown, we are offering a special $50 discount on in-person tickets. Use promo code Autism50 at checkout.

We look forward to welcoming you to San Diego for an unforgettable weekend of education, empowerment, and community.
REGISTER HERE (https://ahsconference.com/pricing-table/?mc_cid=f4f3dce82d&mc_eid=UNIQID)

We are deeply grateful to our top sponsors for their continued support and leadership: Cellular Performance Institute (CPI), TAM Center, Dr. Goodenowe Enterprises, European Wellness, and Satellite Phone Store. Their commitment helps make this event possible and supports ongoing education and outreach within the autism community.

We also extend our sincere thanks to our Silver, Health, and Wellness Sponsors whose generosity and shared mission strengthen this work, including Functional Genomic Analysis, Neuro Needs, Microbiome Research Foundation, NutraMedix, Relax Saunas, MAHA Action, Best EMF Products, ARCC Center, Children's Health Defense, myMico Lab, Life Wave and Brain Tap, Daylight Computer Company, Weston A. Price Foundation, VibraTec Plates, Sun Power LED, Stalwart Law Group, Doniparthi Neurogen Academy, Kadiant, Algonot, Informed Policy Advocates, Micronic Silver, SPELLERS, Spectrum Sciences LLC, The Wellness Blanket, Xlear, Vicar Venetia, Sabre Defense Team, Pur Health, LLC, Warrior Mom, Purium, C-Polar Technologies, OxyHealth, Solex AO Scan, Pulse PEMF, MAPS, PatchMD, NeuroQure, Mindset Kids, and Physicians for Informed Consent.

Most sponsorship levels are sold out, but we have a limited number of Health & Wellness Sponsorships still available for those interested in exhibiting. For more information about becoming a sponsor, email us at info@autismhealth.com (mailto:info@autismhealth.com) .
SPONSORSHIP REGISTRATION (https://ahsconference.com/sponsors/?mc_cid=f4f3dce82d&mc_eid=UNIQID)

New Updates from The Highwire!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=osxchYD7caE&mc_cid=f4f3dce82d&mc_eid=UNIQID

A new interview featuring Tracy Slepcevic, President & Founder of Autism Health, has just been released on The HighWire. In this conversation with Del Bigtree, Tracy shares her personal journey as the mother of a child with autism and discusses how that experience grew into a national advocacy effort supporting families seeking answers and solutions. The interview also explores Tracy’s recent appointment to the Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee within the U.S. Department of HHS, where she will help contribute to conversations shaping the future of autism research, policy development, and federal coordination of autism programs.

During the discussion, Tracy highlights many of the challenges families face today, including regressive autism, environmental influences, co-occurring health conditions, treatment accessibility, and the financial burden many parents experience when therapies are not covered by insurance. She also speaks about her book Warrior Mom: A Mother's Journey in Healing Her Son with Autism, which has served as a resource for parents navigating the autism journey.

The interview also previews the upcoming Autism Health Summit 2026, taking place April 24 to 26 in San Diego. With autism rates continuing to rise, this conversation highlights the growing call for expanded research, transparency, and informed decision-making in children’s health.

Join Us for Our Monthly Webinar!

Join us for an upcoming educational webinar, “Tapping for Autism: A Powerful Approach to Enhance Communication, Connection, and Emotional Regulation,” presented by Lyndsy Moffatt, CGC, taking place Saturday, March 21st at 9:00 AM PST / 12:00 PM EST via Zoom. In this informative session, Lyndsy will introduce families and caregivers to tapping, also known as Emotional Freedom Techniques (EFT), a gentle approach designed to support emotional regulation, reduce stress, and strengthen connection for individuals with autism.

This webinar will explore how tapping can help support communication, calm the nervous system, and create more opportunities for meaningful interaction. Lyndsy will share practical insights and easy-to-understand strategies that parents and caregivers can begin using to help individuals feel more supported and emotionally balanced.

At Autism Health Inc., we are committed to bringing families trusted experts and practical tools that empower them on their journey. This session offers a unique opportunity to learn about a supportive technique that may help improve emotional well-being and strengthen family connections. We hope you’ll join us for this valuable conversation.
REGISTER HERE (https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_QY22rz7GTiix3v5NWt4ajw?mc_cid=f4f3dce82d&mc_eid=UNIQID#/registration)

About Autism Health Inc.
Autism Health is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to educating individuals, families, and communities about autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Autism Health provides educational programs, workshops, events, research, and resources tailored to meet the diverse needs of those impacted by autism and other neurological disorders.
DONATE HERE (https://autismhealth.com/donations/?mc_cid=f4f3dce82d&mc_eid=UNIQID)
Autism Health Inc. depends on generous donations from our community. Large or small, every donation gets us closer to achieving our goals. We are grateful for your assistance! For more information about Autism Health, visit www.AutismHealth.com

For more information about becoming a sponsor, email us at info@autismhealth.com (mailto:info@autismhealth.com) . SPONSORSHIP REGISTRATION () New Updates from The Highwire! A new interview featuring Tracy Slepcevic, President & Founder of Autism Health, has just been released on The HighWire. In this conversation with Del Bigtree, Tracy shares her personal journey as the mother of a child with autism and discusses how that experience grew into a national advocacy effort supporting families seeking answers and solutions. The interview also explores Tracy’s recent appointment to the Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee within the U.S. Department of HHS, where she will help contribute to conversations shaping the future of autism research, policy development, and federal coordination of autism programs. During the discussion, Tracy highlights many of the challenges families face today, including regressive autism, environmental influences, co-occurring health conditions, treatment accessibility, and the financial burden many parents experience when therapies are not covered by insurance. She also speaks about her book Warrior Mom: A Mother's Journey in Healing Her Son with Autism, which has served as a resource for parents navigating the autism journey. The interview also previews the upcoming Autism Health Summit 2026, taking place April 24 to 26 in San Diego. With autism rates continuing to rise, this conversation highlights the growing call for expanded research, transparency, and informed decision-making in children’s health. Join Us for Our Monthly Webinar! Join us for an upcoming educational webinar, “Tapping for Autism: A Powerful Approach to Enhance Communication, Connection, and Emotional Regulation,” presented by Lyndsy Moffatt, CGC, taking place Saturday, March 21st at 9:00 AM PST / 12:00 PM EST via Zoom. In this informative session, Lyndsy will introduce families and caregivers to tapping, also known as Emotional Freedom Techniques (EFT), a gentle approach designed to support emotional regulation, reduce stress, and strengthen connection for individuals with autism. This webinar will explore how tapping can help support communication, calm the nervous system, and create more opportunities for meaningful interaction. Lyndsy will share practical insights and easy-to-understand strategies that parents and caregivers can begin using to help individuals feel more supported and emotionally balanced. At Autism Health Inc., we are committed to bringing families trusted experts and practical tools that empower them on their journey. This session offers a unique opportunity to learn about a supportive technique that may help improve emotional well-being and strengthen family connections. Donald Trump’s Department of Housing and Urban Development is breaking the law, and I’m suing.
Here’s what’s going on:
HUD recently issued guidance telling states we must weaken our housing discrimination protections if we want to keep receiving federal funding to enforce them. We’re talking about protections against discrimination based on race, religion, disability, and more.
Housing is already out of reach for far too many people. Now, the Trump administration is making it harder for people to access a home free from discrimination — and harder for states to hold landlords accountable.
The guidance also threatens to cut off funding for state housing enforcement agencies unless we comply with a list of unrelated political conditions.
It bars agencies from using funds in ways HUD claims “promote” abortion, illegal immigration, or so-called gender ideology — without explaining what they mean by those terms, or how they relate to fair housing protections.
This guidance doesn’t just roll back civil rights progress — it also violates the law. So we’re fighting back in court.
My rule as Attorney General is simple: When the Trump administration breaks the law, I sue. If you’re with me on this, please support our important work with a contribution today. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?amount=50]

subject: Utility costs are unacceptably high
body:

Peter,
Maryland families are seeing skyrocketing utility costs because of the reckless actions of the Trump administration.
**That’s unacceptable -- so we are taking action.**
Together with Maryland Senate President Bill Ferguson and Maryland House Speaker Joseline Peña-Melnyk, I’m introducing a package of legislation aimed at driving down energy bills to make Maryland more affordable and protect our families.
We’ll increase local clean energy production, hold big corporations accountable, and bring prices down for everyone. All together, this will save at least $150 a year while modernizing our entire electric grid.

[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

The cost of living crisis is growing by the day – and now almost a quarter
of Americans can't afford to pay their utility bills in full.

It's not hard to see what's happening: massive new data centers are
popping up across the country – and as demand for electricity skyrockets,
utility companies are passing the cost on to all of us.

Bernie is once again leading the charge to fight back – pushing for a
nationwide moratorium on new data centers – and now more and more
progressives in Congress are standing up with him.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36191?source=email-20260316&t=1011&akid=10398%2E5885482%2Etqf4eo ]Headline: Data center moratorium gains traction among Hill progressives

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36191?source=email-20260316&t=1012&akid=10398%2E5885482%2Etqf4eo ]Momentum is growing, but to force real action, we need massive public
outcry. Will you add your name to stand with Bernie and demand a National
Data Center Moratorium today?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36191?source=email-20260316&t=1013&akid=10398%2E5885482%2Etqf4eo ]ADD YOUR NAME

Artificial intelligence and tech advancements are racing ahead, fueling
profits for tech giants. But communities across the country – and the
world – are paying the price.

>From companies like Anthropic and OpenAI publicly sparing over conditions
for Defense Department work to questions about whether AI was at least in
part to blame for the U.S. hitting a girls elementary school in Iran,
killing 175 civilians, it's clear we need to address how these growing
threats will impact our world.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36191?source=email-20260316&t=1014&akid=10398%2E5885482%2Etqf4eo ]Headline: Democrats ask Pentagon about Iran school strike and role of
AI

At the same time, as new data centers pop up seemingly everywhere,
communities are facing industrial-scale water use draining already scarce
local supply, rising carbon pollution, and constant industrial noise and
loss of land zoned for homes or farms.

These aren't isolated stories. They're a warning about what happens if Big
Tech is allowed to build wherever and whenever it wants. And now Bernie
has a smart proposal to hit pause on the building of new data centers that
are driving up electricity demand.

He's not saying we don't need technology. He's saying we need a plan – and
real protections for people, not profits for Big Tech. Our communities
deserve clean water, affordable power, and a say in what gets built on our
land.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36191?source=email-20260316&t=1015&akid=10398%2E5885482%2Etqf4eo ]Will you sign on now to raise your voice for a national moratorium and

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

clean_body: | | | | | | | | Hi, This is Brigadier General James Emory Mace, U.S. Army (Retired). Today, I write to you not as a soldier... but as a father. I’m a Vietnam War Veteran and Purple Heart Medal recipient. I’ve worn the uniform. I’ve buried friends who never made it home. And I’ve felt the sting of a Nation that sometimes forgets what our sacrifices were for. But my daughter - Congresswoman Nancy Mace - never forgot. Nancy was raised in the shadow of the flag. She saw the uniform. She lived with the deployments. She knew the cost. And instead of running from it, she ran toward it. That’s the kind of person -the kind of fighter \- she is. When Nancy was 17, she dropped out of high school. Most kids in that situation fall apart. But not Nancy. I raised her to believe that setbacks don’t define you -how you rise does. She grew up hearing the same lessons over and over again: 👉 Never quit. 👉 Never run from the truth.👉 And never let anyone tell you thatyou are less than what God made you to be. So I gave her a choice: She picked herself up, took a job at Waffle House, and fought her way back. By 21, she became the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, following in my footsteps. Soon after, she was elected as the first woman to represent South Carolina in the U.S. House of Representatives. She’s been fighting her whole life; for herself, for her kids, for the truth, and now...for her state. Nancy led an evacuation mission in the Middle East after learning a South Carolina family was stranded. Because when your people are stuck in a war zone getting hit with missiles and rockets, the only answer worthy of the office -worthy of our country \- is to get them out. She flew into an active war zone and answered the call when Americans needed help. As a father - and as a Purple Heart Veteran \- I’ve never been more proud of my daughter. That’s why it’s hard when I have to watch Nancy face relentless attacks day after day. Each day that goes out there and fights for you, she’s up against the Establishment’s knife. They stalk her. Send her death threats. She’s even been physically assaulted. But Nancy is my daughter. And I know this: She never backs down. And she never stops fighting. I want to ask you something from one parent, one patriot, to another: Will you support my daughter in the toughest battle of her life? But even in the face of all that, Nancy stood up for me. 👉 She stood up for EVERY veteran who was forgotten. 👉 She stood up for stranded American families and rescued them from an active Middle East warzone.👉 She stood up when other Republicans stayed silent. And now, she’s standing up for YOU. But she needs your backup. I may not wear the uniform anymore, but I still believe in answering the call. Will you answer it with me today? Nancy’s not running to make friends. She’s running to win. To fight. To serve. That’s what she learned growing up in our home. That’s what she learned watching me go off to war. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

# Diesel hits $5+ as Iran War disrupts Hormuz supplies
Diesel prices **[surged past $5 per gallon nationwide](https://substack.com/redirect/0ea35987-1c4c-4e2e-ad00-d36f385ea8f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --the highest since 2022--as the ongoing Iran war halts most tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, triggering the biggest global oil supply disruption in history and driving sharp increases in fuel costs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0ea35987-1c4c-4e2e-ad00-d36f385ea8f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Diesel Surges Dramatically Nationwide:** U.S. diesel averaged $5.04 per gallon on March 17, up 34% from pre-airstrike levels, marking the first time above $5 in over three years amid halted Hormuz shipments.
* **Gasoline Prices Climb Rapidly Too:** Average gas hit $3.79 per gallon, a 27% increase since the war began, with forecasts warning of $4 per gallon soon due to persistent supply pressures.
* **Crude Oil Benchmarks Soar Sharply:** U.S. crude traded near $94 per barrel and Brent around $101, reflecting over 40% gains during the conflict as Iran attacks vessels and blocks key routes.
* **Economic Ripple Effects Intensify:** Trucking and rail firms raise fuel surcharges to offset costs, with analysts predicting continued upward pressure until Hormuz flows resume and disruptions ease.

# Airlines boost Q1 guidance despite Iran War fuel hit
Delta and American Airlines **[raised first-quarter revenue outlooks](https://substack.com/redirect/e19da740-7669-4026-a928-fb3dc2a64578?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** amid the Iran war's fuel price spikes, as strong demand growth offsets roughly $400 million in added expenses from higher jet fuel costs for each carrier.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e19da740-7669-4026-a928-fb3dc2a64578?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Delta Sees Strong Demand Offset:** Delta's bookings rose 25% year-over-year with mid-single-digit unit revenue growth, enabling it to hold original EPS guidance of 50-90 cents despite Q4 fuel hits.
* **American Expects Higher Revenue Jump:** American now projects over 10% total revenue increase (up from 7-10%), citing incredibly strong growth amid industry turbulence and Q1 fuel expense pressures.
* **Fuel Remains Major Cost Pressure:** Jet fuel, airlines' second-largest expense at over 20%, drove $400 million hits for both carriers, though passenger demand and higher fares help mitigate impacts.
* **Stocks React Positively to News:** Delta and American shares gained about 5% in early trading, reflecting investor confidence in demand strength outweighing war-related oil cost challenges.
