# Nvidia eyes $1T orders for Blackwell Vera Rubin
At GTC 2026, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang **[projected up to $1 trillion in orders](https://substack.com/redirect/7cd2868a-1395-466a-9975-662bb36122e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems through 2027, driven by exploding demand for agentic AI and faster inference capabilities.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7cd2868a-1395-466a-9975-662bb36122e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Vera Rubin Delivers Major Efficiency:** Vera Rubin platform, shipping later 2026, offers 10x performance per watt over Grace Blackwell with 1.3 million components in rack-scale systems for AI workloads.
* **Groq Integration Boosts Performance:** Acquired Groq 3 LPU, shipping Q3 2026, unites high-throughput and low-latency processing, boosting Rubin GPUs' tokens per watt by 35 times when combined.
* **Agentic AI Drives Massive Demand:** Shift to agentic apps explodes token generation needs, with Huang noting more capacity directly increases revenues for AI users and developers.
* **Future Kyber Architecture Teased:** Kyber prototype integrates 144 GPUs vertically for higher density and lower latency, set for Vera Rubin Ultra rollout in 2027.

# Mastercard acquires BVNK for $1.8B stablecoin push
Mastercard agreed **[to buy stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK](https://substack.com/redirect/0878b92e-2c2b-4828-807f-3d58b4b23f90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for up to $1.8 billion, accelerating its blockchain payments strategy to enable faster, lower-cost cross-border transfers using digital tokens.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0878b92e-2c2b-4828-807f-3d58b4b23f90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Deal Value Includes Contingents:** Acquisition totals up to $1.8 billion, with $300 million in contingent payments, expected to close before end of 2026.
* **BVNK Bridges Fiat Stablecoins:** BVNK's platform supports payments across major blockchains in over 130 countries, bridging traditional fiat and stablecoins for remittances and business payouts.
* **Mastercard Deepens Crypto Footprint:** Move builds on Crypto Partner Program, positioning Mastercard to compete with Visa in blockchain-based transfers amid growing regulatory clarity.
* **Executive Sees Digital Shift:** Mastercard's chief product officer expects most financial institutions and fintechs to offer digital currency services in time.

# Texas Rare Earth project breaks China Dominance
Texas advances the Round Top deposit--one of North America's richest heavy rare-earth sites--**[to slash U.S. dependence on China for critical minerals](https://substack.com/redirect/10116e6f-ef69-437f-a8c2-6d9737dcc6ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** vital to defense and semiconductors while boosting national security.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/10116e6f-ef69-437f-a8c2-6d9737dcc6ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Round Top Holds Key Heavies:** Deposit contains 15 of 17 rare-earth minerals, heavily weighted in critical "heavies" essential for defense systems, semiconductors, and advanced manufacturing.
* **Texas Leads Domestic Push:** State Commissioner Dawn Buckingham highlights billions in revenue for public schools and efforts to challenge China's global supply chain stronghold.
* **National Security Gains Emphasized:** Project aims to secure domestic processing and supply chains, reducing vulnerabilities and making the U.S. and allies safer from foreign control.
* **USA Rare Earth Accelerates Development:** Company fast-tracks Round Top to build infrastructure, with growing momentum in exploration across West Texas regions.

# Pacific Fleet deploys Gecko wall-climbing and flying robots
The U.S. Pacific Fleet awarded Gecko Robotics a $71 million contract **[to deploy wall-climbing, flying robots](https://substack.com/redirect/68ae06fb-f7e9-4e9c-848b-a76202cb1100?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and AI for faster ship maintenance, inspecting hulls and tanks on 18 vessels up to 50 times quicker.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/68ae06fb-f7e9-4e9c-848b-a76202cb1100?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Robots Enhance Inspection Speed:** Gecko's bots climb hulls, crawl tanks, and fly confined spaces, feeding data to AI Cantilever platform that spots repairs far faster than manual methods.
* **Contract Covers Multiple Ships:** Five-year deal, initial value up to $54 million, targets destroyers, amphibious warships, and littoral combat ships for improved structural assessments.
* **AI Eliminates Maintenance Delays:** One application avoided over three months of flight deck downtime, with Gecko operating 250 robots and planning 50-60 more this year.
* **Navy Boosts Efficiency Fleetwide:** Partnership with GSA focuses on Pacific Fleet readiness through precise, rapid data collection and repair identification.

We have a road map.
Trump showed us how to do it right during the 2024 election.
He went everywhere--Theo Von, Joe Rogan, Nelk Boys--every platform where real people actually spend time.
He didn't cater to the legacy media gatekeepers.
He met voters where they were, and it worked.
If you ask me, we need to learn that lesson fast before 2026.

name: Ken Martin
subject: BREAKING: Democrats deliver yet another stunning upset
body:
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-march-2026?amount=20&refcode=em_20260317_6412_fr&refcode2=6412_22930333_pKY4rC&akid=6412%2E22930333%2EpKY4rC)
---
Derek,
I wanted to make sure you saw this from _the Guardian:_
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-march-2026?amount=20&refcode=em_20260317_6412_fr&refcode2=6412_22930333_pKY4rC&akid=6412%2E22930333%2EpKY4rC)
---
Last week, Democrat Bobbi Boudman won her race for a state legislative seat that Republicans won handily in 2020 and 2024.
But this is no anomaly. Voters are sending a clear message.
Democrats across the country have been winning seismic victories like this one every month — heck, nearly every week — for the past year.
In Arkansas, Alex Holladay won a state house seat held by Republicans for 12 years. In Texas, Taylor Rehmet flipped a 30-year GOP stronghold in a Trump +17 district. In Louisiana, Chasity Verret Martinez defended a tough seat in a Trump +13 district. In total, we’ve flipped 28 state legislative seats since Trump retook office, while Republicans have flipped zero. **None of this happened by accident.**
At the DNC, we’ve made it our job to win from the ground up. We’ve organized, mobilized, and fought for these victories alongside incredible Democratic candidates up and down the ballot.
So, here’s our own message to Donald Trump and MAGA: **no Republican seat is safe.** From now until November, Democrats are going to keep our foot on the gas and compete _everywhere_. Our mission is to retake Congress and take back power across the country.
Rep.-elect Boudman’s campaign proved what Democrats have been demonstrating over and over since Trump took office: While he golfs and builds ballrooms, we’re going to improve lives. Americans see Democrats freezing utility rates, taking on affordable housing, and standing up to Trump’s tariff taxes on everything from groceries to clothes. And when you show up to actually deliver for people, you can win everywhere. Even in ruby-red districts.
But here’s the thing, Derek: If we want to keep winning like this all over the country, we need to continue expanding our campaign infrastructure. From organizing to voter registration, **we need to build the biggest midterm operation in DNC history to take back Congress.**
[**And to build that infrastructure, we need all hands on deck. So, if this work is important to you, can you chip in $7 to the DNC today? We’ll put your donation to work immediately to elect Democrats up and down the ballot, all across the country.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-march-2026?refcode=em_20260317_6412_fr&amount=7&refcode2=6412_22930333_pKY4rC&akid=6412%2E22930333%2EpKY4rC)

As an instructor in Georgia State’s nursing school, I’ve spent years teaching and supporting the students who keep our healthcare system alive. I know how hard they work, how much they sacrifice, and how urgently our state needs more advanced practice nurses — not fewer.
So when I saw this headline...
https://secure.ngpvan.com/4OI02pK92kOTd_uWTjBgFg2 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/4OI02pK92kOTd_uWTjBgFg2]
...I felt sick.
Under Donald Trump’s new proposal, advanced nursing degrees would no longer count as “professional,” meaning students would lose access to the federal loans they need to pursue graduate education. Loan limits would be slashed in half. Thousands of future nurse practitioners, nurse midwives, CRNAs, and clinical nurse specialists could be forced to take on massive private debt — or give up their dreams entirely.
This is not just bad policy.
It’s dangerous — for patients, for hospitals, and for the future of healthcare in this country.
Georgia already faces provider shortages. Rural communities already wait weeks for care. And now Trump wants to create even fewer advanced practice nurses?
We cannot allow this to go unanswered.

# Fun Fact of the Month

name: Voter Action Project Actions
subject: Reversing this USPS change would mean more ballots count this November
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
Public pressure has worked to make USPS reverse course in the recent past. There's every reason to believe we can get them to roll back this awful postmark change before it invalidates countless eligible ballots in the midterm elections.
Make every mail-in vote count by demanding the USPS restore real-time postmarks ASAP! >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/protect-vote-by-mail/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/protect-vote-by-mail/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Folks,
Due to a USPS change, most of the country’s mail dropped in a blue box or handed to a mail carrier on or before an election deadline is no longer guaranteed to receive a real-time postmark. In some cases, postmarks may not be applied for days. That delay can be the difference between a vote that counts and a vote that gets thrown out.
Postmarks are how election officials decide whether a ballot was mailed on time. When postmarks are delayed, ballots become vulnerable to rejection, legal challenges, and partisan games after Election Day. When mail processing is delayed, postmarks lag, and deadlines become murky for voters who tried to do everything right.
This creates a huge risk of opponents of voting rights pushing to discount ballots after the fact.
We must protect vote by mail! Add your name to send a direct message urging your members of Congress to demand the USPS restore real-time postmarks now >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/protect-vote-by-mail/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/protect-vote-by-mail/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
This change is the direct result of former Postmaster General Louis DeJoy’s Regional Transportation Optimization (RTO) plan that quietly went into effect last year.
DeJoy spent years consolidating mail processing out of local communities and centralized it into massive regional hubs that can be hundreds of miles away, sometimes in another state. That means ballots dropped at neighborhood post offices or blue boxes in most of the country are no longer processed locally.
Rural voters and anyone who lives more than 50 miles from one of these mega processing centers are hit hardest – so, most of the country. Many of us rely on mail service for casting our votes, getting prescriptions, paying rent and mortgages, the list goes on. Seniors, veterans, and voters without easy access to in-person voting are especially at risk. Republicans and Democrats alike depend on timely postmarks to ensure their votes count.
The good news is that when it comes to the Postal Service, public pressure works! It worked when we forced DeJoy to pause processing plant consolidation chaos. It worked when Congress intervened to protect election mail in past cycles. It worked when we blocked Trump’s attempt to move the USPS under the control of the Commerce Department and when the administration floated the idea of firing the entire Board of Governors.
Demand the USPS restore real-time postmarks and protect vote by mail today! >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/protect-vote-by-mail/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]

Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

The Irish who came to our part of Pennsylvania did some of the hardest jobs here, especially in the coal region.
They worked hard to make a living and take care of their families and their neighbors. And they led the charge when the owners of mining companies around here screwed over workers and violently tried to keep miners from organizing.
So today we celebrate the Irish Americans in our communities. (And if you started this past weekend, as we did in Pottsville, then good on ya.) But we also honor and remember the ones who came before us.
I've been thinking about my own Irish family history -- how the McGoverns and O'Briens came to Schuylkill County and worked hard here to make a better life for their families despite incredible obstacles.
They were part of a group of people who stood up for themselves and each other as they worked in the mines, fueling the growth of our country. They weren't powerless. They were powerful, because they stood together.
In a way, we are still fighting a version of their fight today -- whether it's [the fight for miners to be protected](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/247eb1ab-f828-4965-990a-68887c3e484c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as they do their jobs, or for communities to be able to control what happens here, not Big Tech or even [the federal government](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/dc86bcce-73c6-4b3e-9f2b-ea9bc06afcd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
We're still looking out for each other, and doing our best to take care of our own.
I'll drink to that -- I hope you will too.

Peter,

Donald Trump promised the American people a pot of gold when he was elected. He was going to bring inflation down, save us all money at the grocery store, protect our benefits, and more. But just like a trickster leprechaun, all those promises were lies–unless you're one of Trump's wealthy friends.

Trump's wealthy friends got massive tax breaks. Trump's wealthy friends aren't the ones dealing with Medicaid losses and healthcare premiums skyrocketing so high that they have to choose between coverage and paying rent. And Trump's wealthy friends aren't the farmers and small business owners whose livelihoods are at risk because of devastating tariffs.

**We all deserve our luck to turn around, but if there's one thing this campaign knows, it's that luck isn't enough to win.**

We have to work hard every day to keep this campaign in fighting shape. We need to invest in our volunteers, save up the resources to run ads and spread our message, and take our future into our own hands. Because even on St. Patrick's Day, we can't hope for our pot of gold to appear under the next rainbow.

Kim is fighting every day for working families. She's protecting our Social Security benefits, lowering healthcare costs, working to put an end to Trump's tariffs, and standing up to extremists who are trying to take us backwards.

Peter –
ICYMI: Donald Trump’s EPA took a dangerous step backward for our country and our planet.
They rolled back the Endangerment Finding – the 2009 determination that greenhouse gas pollution endangers public health and welfare. It may sound technical, but it’s actually the legal backbone that allows the EPA to limit climate pollution.
And this isn’t up for debate. But Trump’s EPA is ignoring the law.
Instead, they’re gutting climate protections and rewarding big oil and gas companies – all while communities across Colorado and the country face worsening wildfires, drought, and extreme weather.
Let’s be clear: science doesn’t lie.
Climate pollution is real.
The harm is real.
And working people pay the price first and worst.
We cannot allow the federal government to abandon its responsibility to protect our air, our water, and our future.
Because clean air and clean water are not political – they are a human right. But taking on powerful interests and a federal administration willing to break the law requires a strong campaign behind this fight.
If you’re able, please chip in today to help power this campaign and our work to protect Colorado families and our climate. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2603-q1-jg?refcode=260317-email]
Thank you for standing with me.

clean_body: [] Peter – ICYMI: Donald Trump’s EPA took a dangerous step backward for our country and our planet. They rolled back the Endangerment Finding – the 2009 determination that greenhouse gas pollution endangers public health and welfare. It may sound technical, but it’s actually the legal backbone that allows the EPA to limit climate pollution. And this isn’t up for debate. But Trump’s EPA is ignoring the law. Instead, they’re gutting climate protections and rewarding big oil and gas companies – all while communities across Colorado and the country face worsening wildfires, drought, and extreme weather. Let’s be clear: science doesn’t lie. Climate pollution is real. The harm is real. And working people pay the price first and worst. We cannot allow the federal government to abandon its responsibility to protect our air, our water, and our future. Because clean air and clean water are not political – they are a human right. But taking on powerful interests and a federal administration willing to break the law requires a strong campaign behind this fight. Joining me is Jerome Conlon Author of Brand Soul Bridges: The Human Centered Use of Ai & the Craft of Designing with Light. Jerome is a visionary strategic marketing executive, using agile multi-visioning methods, with a 25-year track record of revitalizing global brands through innovative planning and problem-solving. Directed Nike's brand planning during a 10x sales surge (from $860M to $6.6B), spearheaded Starbucks' 3x growth via channel expansion, and launched NBC hits like The West Wing and Will & Grace, pioneering the Reality TV genre. As author of The Brand Bridge and Soulful Branding on brand strategy, Jerome brings unique frameworks that drive transformative growth, evidenced by 400% enrollment growth at Full Sail University as a consultant. Jerome is adept at integrating consumer insights with creative execution to reclaim market dominance and inspire industry shifts and has a lot to share regarding the role AI plays in our life.
Jerome Conlon is the Founder of The Field Harmonix Institute. Field Harmonix Resonance ScanningTM is the world's first coherence-based diagnostic system for stories, brands, leaders, and creative works. For more about Jerome visit him at

**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
| | Hi friends,
Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.joinrmv.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.). And also, check out our [deep-dive video of the day on TABOR!](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏛️ **Under the Golden Dome...** Democrat-backed tax bills are drawing scrutiny for proposals to [“decouple” the state tax code from federal deductions](https://link.email.joinrmv.) (a TABOR workaround), while lawmakers advanced a housing bill allowing some projects on public land to [bypass local hearings and control](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Debate also continues over a measure letting large energy users [build their own power systems](https://link.email.joinrmv.) instead of relying on ratepayer-funded utilities, as lawmakers consider [eliminating most interim committees](https://link.email.joinrmv.) to save roughly $396,000 in a tight budget year.

🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** The Cover All Coloradans program is now projected to cost $104.5 million—[more than six times initial estimates](https://link.email.joinrmv.)—adding pressure to the state budget. A Colorado eye surgeon appointed to a federal EPA advisory panel is [defending his qualifications](https://link.email.joinrmv.), while [Republican U.S. Senate candidate George Markert](https://link.email.joinrmv.), a retired Marine colonel, is emphasizing his national security background in his challenge to Sen. John Hickenlooper.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** A Minnesota elections official acknowledged [noncitizens could potentially cast ballots under current systems](https://link.email.joinrmv.), as Senate Republicans prepare for a [high-profile debate on the SAVE America Act](https://link.email.joinrmv.) requiring proof of citizenship to vote. A North Dakota ruling ordering Greenpeace to [pay major damages tied to pipeline protests](https://link.email.joinrmv.) could threaten the group financially, while the Trump administration is moving to [stabilize energy markets during the Iran conflict](https://link.email.joinrmv.) through coordinated oil releases and expanded U.S. production.
This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, March 17, 2026. 🍀
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado Senate advances bill limiting local control over housing projects](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
Colorado lawmakers spent part of the week hashing out just how much the state should push new housing.
The Senate approved [House Bill 26-1001](https://link.email.joinrmv.)—after several amendments. Those amendments were agreed upon by the House the next day.
Land that is already owned by institutions or the government is the main focus of the bill. If the measure is eventually passed into law, property owned by school districts, housing authorities, universities, transit agencies, and some nonprofit organizations may be eligible for a simplified approval process.
Supporters say some of that property is sitting unused. If approvals were easier, they argue, some of it could be turned into housing.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**

**[George Markert is running for U.S. Senate. He’s already been in the room.](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Retired Marine colonel launches U.S. Senate bid:** George Markert, a 30-year Marine Corps veteran, is running against Sen. John Hickenlooper, citing a family legacy of military service and a commitment to defending the Constitution.

* **Campaign built on national security experience:** Markert points to years at U.S. Central Command and multiple Middle East deployments, saying his firsthand experience with conflicts and military planning gives him insight into current global threats.

* **Criticizes leadership on border, energy, and security:** Markert argues current leadership has shown “inaction” on key issues including border policy, energy, and law enforcement, and says stronger oversight and accountability are needed in Washington.

**[House Bill 26-1246: Protecting Colorado’s citizens, landscape, and economy](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY REP. KEN DEGRAAF, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Bill targets rising energy costs tied to utility incentives:** House Bill 26-1246 responds to a system where utilities earn guaranteed returns on large infrastructure projects, with costs passed on to ratepayers through higher electricity bills.

* **Would allow large users to build their own power systems:** The proposal permits major energy consumers—such as data centers—to develop private, self-funded generation separate from the public grid, avoiding reliance on utility-built infrastructure.

* **Supporters say it protects ratepayers and limits expansion impacts:** Backers argue the approach could reduce costs for households, limit large-scale transmission projects affecting land and water resources, and help Colorado compete for major industrial investment.

**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | NATIONAL | MARCH 11** _The New York Times ran its verdict last week on Dr. Brian C. Joondeph’s EPA appointment. Just an eye doctor. Kyle Clark said the same thing. Joondeph is a Colorado retina surgeon and political commentator. Trump’s EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin tapped him for the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee—CASAC. The Times piece, published March 12, went after his qualifications: no air-pollution peer-reviewed research, not a climate scientist, wrong kind of doctor._ __
**[Special edition: The Iranian War — the fiery darts of war](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)****BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | MARCH 15** _I understand war. Not just as a headline or political talking point, but as someone who spent over twenty years in active duty military service and now lives with a 70% service-connected disability as a vet. During those years, wars came and went — Desert Storm, Afghanistan, Iraq, and countless endless conflicts that most Americans eventually stopped paying attention to. But when you serve long enough, you realize something: war is never just about nations. It is about human hearts._

**🍀 DID YOU KNOW?** **St. Patrick’s Day (March 17) honors Ireland’s patron saint, but much of the story is myth.** He was likely born in Britain, not Ireland, and was kidnapped and brought there as a slave before later returning as a missionary. He’s commonly associated with green today, but blue was the original color linked to him, with green gaining popularity much later. The famous tale of him driving out snakes is symbolic—Ireland never had snakes due to its climate. Traditions like wearing green, parades, and shamrocks—said to represent the Holy Trinity—developed over time.

Joining me is Mike Smith the man depicted in the new movie Gutter Gospel. As a fractured world grapples with an unprecedented mental health epidemic, a voice from the pavement is rising to offer a radical kind of medicine. Mike is that voice and he is using his hard learned lessons to help others escape the hell they have found themselves in.
To put in in Mikes words "Most people see the gutter as a dead end, but I found it was a sanctuary where God finally got my attention," says the film's subject. "We are living in a Luke 16 world where people are chasing comfort while their souls are starving. This movie shows that while the 'great gulf' is real, the bridge built in John 3:16 is still open for anyone."
The film's narrative is centered on a powerful, biographical truth: "After hitting rock bottom in the streets of North Dakota, a broken man discovers that his greatest setback was actually a divine setup to launch a global ministry feeding the hungry and the hopeless." This is a story of hunger, hope, and the ultimate pivot that has already resonated far beyond the American heartland. The "Gutter Gospel" message has achieved a staggering 200-country reach, proving that the struggle for mental clarity and spiritual peace is a universal human experience. From the frozen streets of Fargo to the farthest corners of the globe, this message provides a lifeline to those who feel invisible.
You will not want to miss this riveting interview with a man who has been through hell and back and is now helping others find new life and meaning through the Gospel of Jesus Christ. For more about Mike and his journey go to
https://theguttergospel.com/

body:
| | |
As the 2026 legislative session comes to a close in Richmond, I am writing to share with you the progress we’ve made and the fight that lies ahead. When you elected me to represent the 22nd District, you sent a working mother, a social worker, and a lifelong advocate for working families and public education. I carried that responsibility with me every single day. I carried 12 bills this session–each one focused on the people I represent: working families, immigrant families, students, veterans, and everyone who has ever wondered if the system was built for them. I was proud to be selected to serve on the House Education, General Laws, and Transportation Committees, working across subcommittees like Housing/Consumer Protection and Early Childhood Innovation to ensure our laws work for everyone. It is important to mention that these bills were recommended by you while I was knocking on doors: **Supporting Our Students and Families:** **HB 413: High School Certified Nurse Aide Training/Certification Program** This bill establishes a program to train high-school students as Certified Nurse Aides (CNAs), creating a direct pipeline to good-paying jobs in healthcare, right after high school graduation. Students will be able to earn the certification before they graduate. **HB 414: Two-Year College Transfer Grant** This bill expands access to higher education by removing the Selective Service question for the Two-Year College Transfer Grant and the Virginia Tuition Assistance Grant Program, to align with federal law. This bill will expand opportunities for students to access state grants. **HB 417: Reducing the Years for Military Families to Receive In-State Tuition:** Something I heard on the doors often was the 10 year minimum requirement of Virginia Tax returns it takes for military families to receive in-state tuition. Every other family gets in-state tuition after 2 years. This bill would allow our service members and their families to access state tuition at the 4 year mark. **HB 495: Mental Health Awareness Training for School Bus Drivers** We know mental health challenges don’t stop at the school door. This bill ensures our school bus drivers–the first adults many children see in the morning–have the training to recognize and respond to any student in distress. While this bill didn’t make it across the finish line in the Senate, I will keep fighting for this in future sessions, because our children deserve to have the support system they need to thrive. **HB 497: Special Education Data Collection** To ensure we are meeting the needs of students with disabilities, this bill requires the collection of better data on special education services. The amount of IEP denials and complaints due to compliance is not collected anywhere. This bill will help identify and improve services. **HB 955: SCHEV Reporting** This bill directs SCHEV to compile a report of all in-state, out of state, and international students. This data will be crucial to helping the Education Committee take action to ensure that Virginia Students are given a fair shot to stay in Virginia if they choose. **HB 957: Student Bullying Tipline** This bill would direct school boards to promote the 988 suicide tipline to support students who are being bullied or cyberbullied so they can access trained professionals to assist potentially accessing professional counseling to address emotional trauma and build resilience. **HB 1404: Local Government Youth Representative** This bill would allow localities to adopt a law to allow a student ages 15-17, as a non-voting youth member of the local city or county board. This expands a law that was passed to allow them to participate on local schools boards. **Helping our Neighbors, Federal Workers:** **HB 494: Hiring Preference in State Government for Certain Former Federal Employees** With all the uncertainty coming out of Washington, federal workers in Virginia are being left behind. This bill gives them an opportunity to stay in public service and obtain state employment as long as they meet the qualifications for the job they are applying for. **Protecting Our Communities and Environment:** **HB 496: Water Use Disclosures for Data Centers** As data centers rapidly expand in our region, this bill fights for transparency by authorizing a locality to include in its zoning ordinance provisions requiring industrial and commercial facilities to submit annual water consumption estimates and consideration of water consumption from public resources, protecting our environment and ensuring sustainable growth that respects residential communities. **1502: Data Center Generators** As data centers rapidly expand in our region, this bill studies the pollutants, their levels, and makes recommendations to the Committee on Agriculture and Natural resources on ways to address these pollutants. This is a critical first step in getting the data we need to make informed decisions. **THANK YOU**
* * *
**Early Vote for the Redistricting Amendment is Here!** The proposed amendment would give the General Assembly the authority to redraw one or more of Virginia's congressional districts before 2031, in limited circumstances. In the event that another state redraws its own congressional districts before 2031, without being ordered by a court to do so, the General Assembly would then be able to redraw Virginia's congressional districts. The General Assembly's power to do so would continue until October 31, 2030, and the Virginia Redistricting Commission would reassume the responsibility of drawing the congressional districts in 2031. **The start of early voting for the April 21st election on the redistricting constitutional amendment is here.**

clean_body: | | | As the 2026 legislative session comes to a close in Richmond, I am writing to share with you the progress we’ve made and the fight that lies ahead. When you elected me to represent the 22nd District, you sent a working mother, a social worker, and a lifelong advocate for working families and public education. I carried that responsibility with me every single day. I carried 12 bills this session–each one focused on the people I represent: working families, immigrant families, students, veterans, and everyone who has ever wondered if the system was built for them. I was proud to be selected to serve on the House Education, General Laws, and Transportation Committees, working across subcommittees like Housing/Consumer Protection and Early Childhood Innovation to ensure our laws work for everyone. It is important to mention that these bills were recommended by you while I was knocking on doors: Supporting Our Students and Families: HB 413: High School Certified Nurse Aide Training/Certification Program This bill establishes a program to train high-school students as Certified Nurse Aides (CNAs), creating a direct pipeline to good-paying jobs in healthcare, right after high school graduation. Students will be able to earn the certification before they graduate. HB 414: Two-Year College Transfer Grant This bill expands access to higher education by removing the Selective Service question for the Two-Year College Transfer Grant and the Virginia Tuition Assistance Grant Program, to align with federal law. This bill will expand opportunities for students to access state grants. HB 417: Reducing the Years for Military Families to Receive In-State Tuition: Something I heard on the doors often was the 10 year minimum requirement of Virginia Tax returns it takes for military families to receive in-state tuition. Every other family gets in-state tuition after 2 years. This bill would allow our service members and their families to access state tuition at the 4 year mark. HB 495: Mental Health Awareness Training for School Bus Drivers We know mental health challenges don’t stop at the school door. This bill ensures our school bus drivers–the first adults many children see in the morning–have the training to recognize and respond to any student in distress. While this bill didn’t make it across the finish line in the Senate, I will keep fighting for this in future sessions, because our children deserve to have the support system they need to thrive. HB 497: Special Education Data Collection To ensure we are meeting the needs of students with disabilities, this bill requires the collection of better data on special education services. The amount of IEP denials and complaints due to compliance is not collected anywhere. This bill will help identify and improve services. HB 955: SCHEV Reporting This bill directs SCHEV to compile a report of all in-state, out of state, and international students. This data will be crucial to helping the Education Committee take action to ensure that Virginia Students are given a fair shot to stay in Virginia if they choose. HB 957: Student Bullying Tipline This bill would direct school boards to promote the 988 suicide tipline to support students who are being bullied or cyberbullied so they can access trained professionals to assist potentially accessing professional counseling to address emotional trauma and build resilience. HB 1404: Local Government Youth Representative This bill would allow localities to adopt a law to allow a student ages 15-17, as a non-voting youth member of the local city or county board. This expands a law that was passed to allow them to participate on local schools boards. Helping our Neighbors, Federal Workers: HB 494: Hiring Preference in State Government for Certain Former Federal Employees With all the uncertainty coming out of Washington, federal workers in Virginia are being left behind. This bill gives them an opportunity to stay in public service and obtain state employment as long as they meet the qualifications for the job they are applying for. Protecting Our Communities and Environment: HB 496: Water Use Disclosures for Data Centers As data centers rapidly expand in our region, this bill fights for transparency by authorizing a locality to include in its zoning ordinance provisions requiring industrial and commercial facilities to submit annual water consumption estimates and consideration of water consumption from public resources, protecting our environment and ensuring sustainable growth that respects residential communities. 1502: Data Center Generators As data centers rapidly expand in our region, this bill studies the pollutants, their levels, and makes recommendations to the Committee on Agriculture and Natural resources on ways to address these pollutants. This is a critical first step in getting the data we need to make informed decisions. THANK YOU Early Vote for the Redistricting Amendment is Here! The proposed amendment would give the General Assembly the authority to redraw one or more of Virginia's congressional districts before 2031, in limited circumstances. In the event that another state redraws its own congressional districts before 2031, without being ordered by a court to do so, the General Assembly would then be able to redraw Virginia's congressional districts. Friend, today is primary election day in Illinois. **AIPAC and its allies have spent $22 million on these elections.**
It should surprise no one that the group that spent **_$126 million_** in the 2024 election cycle to defeat progressives would be back again, trying to influence our Democratic primaries.
One anonymous source told _Politico_ : “Our primary goal in Illinois is to prevent potential ‘Squad’ members from being elected to Congress.”
But here’s the thing. Defending Israel’s criminal, genocidal, war-obsessed regime is harder than ever for folks like AIPAC. Public opinion has turned sharply away from Israel as we’ve rallied support for the dignity and self-determination of Palestinians.
So, AIPAC has learned to funnel their mostly Republican donor money into Democratic primaries by moving it into new, generic-sounding PACs such as “Elect Chicago Women”, which has been spending big on TV and digital ads in Illinois in the past weeks. These ads aren’t even about the issue of Israel — they instead hit progressives from the left to generate infighting and confuse voters.
**This is a complete subversion of our democracy and a danger to the success of our progressive movement across the country.**
Here in Minneapolis, I now have two credible challengers who have announced they are running against me in the Democratic primary. At any moment, AIPAC could swoop in with a new generic PAC and dump millions and millions of dollars into vicious attack ads against me on any issue they think will do damage.

Our collective power is stronger than their fight to separate us. | | | Peter, **United We Dream is rooted in uniting ALL young people around what we can build together because the fight for immigrant rights and dignity belongs to all of us.** This has never been more evident than in the past few months as DHS turned its force against citizens. According to the Wall Street Journal1, official DHS social media accounts called out 279 people for assault. Of those, 181 were U.S. citizens who were never convicted, charged with a crime, or detained. Yet, many have had their private information leaked to the public and had to answer for their peaceful protest. We know our neighbors are builders and creators who power this country every day. **And we’ve seen how strong we are when we work together and take care of one another.** **We, the people, hold the power in our hands!** Together, we can uplift one another and tackle the challenges our communities face. From advocating for affordable housing to keeping grocery prices fair, and standing against police and ICE injustices, our communities across the nation are grappling with the same issues.**While we might not see eye to eye on every solution, one thing is crystal clear: we’re stronger together.** **Let’s harness our power and build a better future where everyone is free to live, speak, and be themselves.** [**If you’re inspired by what we’ve accomplished together and believe in what we can continue to build, can you make a donation to United We Dream today? This has never been more evident than in the past few months as DHS turned its force against citizens. According to the Wall Street Journal1, official DHS social media accounts called out 279 people for assault. Of those, 181 were U.S. citizens who were never convicted, charged with a crime, or detained. Yet, many have had their private information leaked to the public and had to answer for their peaceful protest. We know our neighbors are builders and creators who power this country every day. And we’ve seen how strong we are when we work together and take care of one another. We, the people, hold the power in our hands! name: Tim Kaine
subject: Why I’m supporting a YES vote on Virginia’s redistricting amendment
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Virginians for Fair Elections
body:
Virginia voters have the opportunity to make sure our elections stay in the hands of the people, not politicians.
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260317-344&t=1&akid=344%2E12592%2Eilgajy)
Friends,
Donald Trump has made it clear that he’s willing to bend, break, or bulldoze democratic norms if it helps him cling to power.
Now, with the midterm elections coming up, Virginia voters have the opportunity to make sure elections stay in the hands of the people, not politicians.
**_Critically, the upcoming referendum gives _voters_ the right to decide what comes next._**
I’m supporting a YES vote on Virginia’s redistricting amendment because I believe this will restore fairness in our elections and prevent Donald Trump from locking in power months before November.
[**If you’re on board, I’m asking you to join me in supporting Virginians for Fair Elections. They’re working around the clock to reach voters across the Commonwealth with clear, factual information about what this amendment does and why it matters. Will you contribute whatever amount is meaningful to you today?**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260317_1.ukORsY&amount=3&refcode=20260317-344&t=2&akid=344%2E12592%2Eilgajy)
**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260317_1.ukORsY&amount=3&refcode=20260317-344&t=21&akid=344%2E12592%2Eilgajy)**
This election is happening on April 21, not in November.
**That means time is running out for the ballot measure committee to reach voters with important education and information.**
The stakes are incredibly high in 2026, and Virginia voters have a serious responsibility in front of us to consider this redistricting amendment and make our choice about what happens next. Unlike other states around the country pushing redistricting, this decision will be made directly by the people of our Commonwealth.
[************If you’re with me on this** , I hope you’ll consider donating to support Virginians for Fair Elections today. I believe this amendment will safeguard Virginia’s elections ahead of this year’s crucial midterm elections. **](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260317_1.ukORsY&amount=3&refcode=20260317-344&t=22&akid=344%2E12592%2Eilgajy)
Thank you for standing up for our democracy.
Tim Kaine
U.S. Senator for Virginia

# Remembering Captain Seth R Koval
---
|
---
| | Hello everyone. As many of you heard the Mooresville and Indiana community were truly shocked to hear about Captain Seth Koval tragic passing in the line of duty over Iraq this past weekend. Seth was a man of faith who grew up in my hometown of Mooresville. Seth served this country with honor and his memory and sacrifice defending our country will not go forgotten. He unfortunately leaves behind a young son and his wife Heather who both cherished him fondly. I am writing this email today to let you know about a great Gofundme going directly to his wife and family and I ask that you keep them in your prayers and possibly contribute if have the means to donate to them. Thank you Seth for your service and God Bless America.

His letter says Iran posed no imminent threat and that this administration was manipulated into it by high-ranking Israeli officials and their allies in American media. subject: Public service means serving everyone
body:
Not just the people who voted for you

| |

Hi friend, When you win an election, you don’t just represent the people who voted for you. You represent everyone. That’s democracy. When a constituent comes to me with a problem, I don’t ask them who they voted for. I don’t ask them to prove they support me. I listen. And then I work to solve the problem. But MAGA Republicans are taking a very different approach. They’ve made loyalty their number one priority. Loyalty above country. Loyalty above the Constitution. Loyalty above the needs of everyday Americans. We’ve seen it again and again. If you don’t pledge allegiance to them, they won’t fight for you. That’s not how our democracy is supposed to work. clean_body: Not just the people who voted for you | | Hi friend, When you win an election, you don’t just represent the people who voted for you. You represent everyone. That’s democracy. When a constituent comes to me with a problem, I don’t ask them who they voted for. I don’t ask them to prove they support me. I listen. And then I work to solve the problem. But MAGA Republicans are taking a very different approach. They’ve made loyalty their number one priority. Loyalty above country. Loyalty above the Constitution. Loyalty above the needs of everyday Americans. We’ve seen it again and again. If you don’t pledge allegiance to them, they won’t fight for you. That’s not how our democracy is supposed to work. We need to reject this toxic way of thinking and build a government that serves everyone, regardless of party. body:
Let me cut to the chase.
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/221?c0=em_ms_cp_20260317_2.mB64iO&refcode=em20260317-2&t=26&akid=5622%2E582294%2EPv7iub)
JB Pritzker here.
Let me cut to the chase: **New Hampshire’s Senate race could decide whether Democrats take back the majority — _and Republicans know it._**
Donald Trump and the MAGA GOP see this seat as one of their best shots to expand their power.
They’ve already got a Republican governor in New Hampshire, and they’re betting they can flip the Senate seat next. If they win here, our chances of taking back the Senate drop to zero.
_We can’t let that happen._
Chris Pappas is a proven fighter for working families — taking on Big Pharma, defending reproductive freedom, and making sure our government actually works for the people it serves.
I’ve seen what happens when leaders like Chris have the platform and the power to make change — and _I want him in the Senate._
I know Chris can win, but there’s no way around it: **_This isn’t a safe blue seat, folks._**
The GOP is ready to flood New Hampshire with attack ads and dark money. The only way to beat them is with early, grassroots support. That’s where you come in:
**[If you can, please make a $20.26 donation right now to help Chris Pappas win in New Hampshire and put Democrats on the path to a Senate majority.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/221?c0=em_ms_cp_20260317_2.mB64iO&refcode=em20260317-2&t=27&akid=5622%2E582294%2EPv7iub)**

subject: They Think This Seat Is Easy to Flip

body:
I was officially designated a top target by House Democrats. Now, House Democrat Leader Hakeem Jeffries is saying they “expect to have an extension level event” as part of their effort to take back the Majority. | Fellow American - I don’t have good news.

_**FIRST:**_ I was officially named a top target by House Democrats (DCCC)

_**NOW:**_ House Democrat Leader Hakeem Jeffries says they “expect to have an extinction level event” as part of their effort to take back the Majority.

body:
Peter,

Earlier this month, I traveled to New Hampshire to spend time talking with workers at a local union hall.

I visited the AFL-CIO headquarters in Hooksett, where I sat down with union members and answered their questions about the issues that matter most to them.

If there's one thing I know, it's that **unions built the middle class, and it's something that too many politicians in Washington seem to forget.**

For generations, organized labor has fought to make sure working people could earn a fair wage, afford healthcare, and build a better life for their families. And those fights are just as important today as they've ever been. The leaders and candidates I met with in New Hampshire understand that all too well.

They're standing up for the middle class, proudly supporting unions, and fighting to make sure working Americans finally get their fair share. Those are the kinds of leaders that In This Together PAC is working to elect — leaders who aren't running for office to empower their billionaire friends or protect special interests.

**Now, more than ever before, we need leaders who understand that when working families succeed, our whole country succeeds.** And I'm traveling the country to support candidates who know exactly that, and who won't hesitate to stand with workers and fight for the middle class. But building the kind of momentum we need to spread my message across the country takes resources.

clean_body: Peter, Earlier this month, I traveled to New Hampshire to spend time talking with workers at a local union hall. I visited the AFL-CIO headquarters in Hooksett, where I sat down with union members and answered their questions about the issues that matter most to them. If there's one thing I know, it's that unions built the middle class, and it's something that too many politicians in Washington seem to forget. For generations, organized labor has fought to make sure working people could earn a fair wage, afford healthcare, and build a better life for their families. And those fights are just as important today as they've ever been. The leaders and candidates I met with in New Hampshire understand that all too well. They're standing up for the middle class, proudly supporting unions, and fighting to make sure working Americans finally get their fair share. Those are the kinds of leaders that In This Together PAC is working to elect — leaders who aren't running for office to empower their billionaire friends or protect special interests. Now, more than ever before, we need leaders who understand that when working families succeed, our whole country succeeds. And I'm traveling the country to support candidates who know exactly that, and who won't hesitate to stand with workers and fight for the middle class. name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I’ve never believed in wasting money
body:
Here’s how this campaign really works.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I want to tell you a little about how this campaign actually operates — because it says a lot about how I’ll lead as governor.
I’ve never believed in wasting money. That’s not a campaign talking point; it’s how I’ve lived my whole life. When you grow up watching every dollar, you learn quickly that money represents someone’s time, sacrifice, and trust.
That mindset shapes every decision we make.
We’re building a campaign powered by people, not billionaires.
We focus on what helps us win: organizing communities, talking directly with voters, and showing up everywhere — not just where it’s convenient.
Sometimes that means long drives instead of flights. El Paso to Austin? No problem. It means reusing placards after events, meeting in libraries or community centers instead of expensive venues. Most of all, it means knowing we’re accountable for how we spend what supporters like you give.
I know how much a contribution can mean — especially right now. When someone decides to give, that’s an act of trust. I don’t take that lightly for a second.
**[Peter, if you’re able to pitch in $5 today, you’ll be helping us keep building a campaign that’s disciplined, people-powered, and strong enough to defeat Greg Abbott.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260317_1_thrifty.kNkXUi&refcode=em20260317-771&amount=5&t=1&akid=771%2E299639%2Eg4qap4)**

Thank you for standing with me. I’m truly grateful to be in this fight with you.
— Gina

Chuck Rocha and Mike Madrid welcomed a guest who sits at the very center of Latino political and cultural life in America: **Daniel Alegre, CEO of TelevisaUnivision** , the largest Spanish-language media company in the United States. What followed was one of the most data-rich, candid, and consequential conversations the podcast has produced to date.

* * *
### The Poll: Affordability Above Everything
[Check out TelevisaUnivision's New Poll](https://substack.com/redirect/ad0343e8-3c13-4498-88a6-6e796e8a0dd9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
TelevisaUnivision, in partnership with the Harris polling firm, conducted a new survey of Latino voters, including those who had just cast ballots in the recent Texas elections, and the findings leave little room for interpretation.

76% of Latino respondents identified the cost of living and inflation as their most pressing concern. Not abortion. Not foreign policy. Not Greenland. Groceries. Rent. Healthcare. The pocketbook issues that hit working Latino families hardest.
"That was issue number one, issue number two, and issue number three," Alegre said plainly. "Everything else was absolutely secondary."
The poll also found that 82% of Latino voters now believe their vote is a critically decisive factor in American elections -- a sign that the community is not only growing in size but in political self-awareness. And perhaps the most staggering data point of the conversation: 50% of all new voter registrations in the United States are Hispanic. A number, as Madrid noted, that is still accelerating.
* * *
### The Message Is Still Not Getting Through
Despite the data, Alegre points out how many campaigns continue to miss the mark. He described sitting with senior advisors from major 2024 campaigns and listening to them outline their Latino outreach strategies, only to find them anchored in issues that simply did not reflect what Latino communities were actually talking about.
"I said, I don't think you're listening," Alegre recalled of one such meeting. "Affordability, affordability, and affordability. That's what they care about."
The mistakes, he explained, tend to follow a predictable pattern. Campaigns wait until the final two weeks to begin outreach. They assume a Spanish surname on a staffer's business card is a substitute for genuine community engagement. They advertise on English-language media and wonder why the message doesn't stick. And they rely on broad demographic assumptions that have been disproven election cycle after election cycle.
"The definition of insanity," Alegre said, "is doing the same thing over and over and expecting a different result."
* * *
### What Getting It Right Actually Looks Like
Alegre, Rocha, and Madrid all pointed to Ted Cruz's 2024 Senate race as a case study in effective Latino outreach. Cruz advertised in both English and Spanish, tailored his message to issues Latino voters actually cared about, showed up personally to Spanish-language media, despite not being a fluent Spanish speaker, and built his Latino engagement over time rather than in a last-minute sprint. He won.
Ruben Gallego's Arizona Senate race was cited as another model. Rocha, who served as a senior advisor on the campaign, described an intentional, early, and layered approach to Spanish-language advertising that drove meaningful overperformance with Latino voters.
And then there was James Talarico in Texas: a candidate who engaged the Latino community early, showed up at the events and cultural moments that matter, and won every single Latino precinct he needed.
* * *
### The 2026 Battleground
Then they turned to the races that will define the next chapter of Latino political power in America. Chuck and Mike set the stage for the 2026 battleground: the wide-open California Governor's race, where Latino voters could determine the outcome of a crowded field; the Texas Governor and Senate races; an Arizona Governor's race; a competitive Florida Senate race; and a string of targeted congressional seats along the Texas Rio Grande Valley and in Miami, where a new high-profile candidate just entered the race.
Alegre's message to any candidate running in any of these states was consistent: do not assume the Latino vote is coming to you. Go earn it. Go earn it now.
He also revealed a striking data point from the Texas election cycle: one in five Latino voters in their survey recalled seeing a Spanish-language political ad. **That means roughly 25% of Latino voters were completely unreached by any political message whatsoever.**
"Twenty-five percent," Alegre said. "That's who you're leaving on the table."
* * *
### The VIX Factor: Reaching the Next Generation
For campaigns thinking about digital outreach, Alegre offered a critical distinction. Algorithms on platforms like Facebook or YouTube may flag someone as Hispanic because they watched a Bad Bunny video. That data, he argued, is fundamentally unreliable.
TelevisaUnivision's streaming platform VIX -- currently the fastest-growing subscription streaming service in the United States -- operates differently. If someone is on VIX, Alegre said, there is a 99.9% probability they are Hispanic. The platform's targeting, combined with TelevisaUnivision's household data graph that aggregates local TV, national TV, radio, digital, and third-party sources, gives campaigns the most precise Latino targeting available anywhere in the media landscape.
"If you want to find a Hispanic voter," Alegre said plainly, "we'll deliver them for you."

Not foreign policy. Not Greenland. Groceries. Rent. Healthcare. The pocketbook issues that hit working Latino families hardest. "That was issue number one, issue number two, and issue number three," Alegre said plainly. "Everything else was absolutely secondary." The poll also found that 82% of Latino voters now believe their vote is a critically decisive factor in American elections -- a sign that the community is not only growing in size but in political self-awareness. And perhaps the most staggering data point of the conversation: 50% of all new voter registrations in the United States are Hispanic. A number, as Madrid noted, that is still accelerating. The Message Is Still Not Getting Through Despite the data, Alegre points out how many campaigns continue to miss the mark. He described sitting with senior advisors from major 2024 campaigns and listening to them outline their Latino outreach strategies, only to find them anchored in issues that simply did not reflect what Latino communities were actually talking about. "I said, I don't think you're listening," Alegre recalled of one such meeting. "Affordability, affordability, and affordability. That's what they care about." The mistakes, he explained, tend to follow a predictable pattern. Campaigns wait until the final two weeks to begin outreach. They assume a Spanish surname on a staffer's business card is a substitute for genuine community engagement. They advertise on English-language media and wonder why the message doesn't stick. And they rely on broad demographic assumptions that have been disproven election cycle after election cycle. "The definition of insanity," Alegre said, "is doing the same thing over and over and expecting a different result." What Getting It Right Actually Looks Like Alegre, Rocha, and Madrid all pointed to Ted Cruz's 2024 Senate race as a case study in effective Latino outreach. Cruz advertised in both English and Spanish, tailored his message to issues Latino voters actually cared about, showed up personally to Spanish-language media, despite not being a fluent Spanish speaker, and built his Latino engagement over time rather than in a last-minute sprint. He won. Ruben Gallego's Arizona Senate race was cited as another model. Rocha, who served as a senior advisor on the campaign, described an intentional, early, and layered approach to Spanish-language advertising that drove meaningful overperformance with Latino voters. And then there was James Talarico in Texas: a candidate who engaged the Latino community early, showed up at the events and cultural moments that matter, and won every single Latino precinct he needed. The 2026 Battleground Then they turned to the races that will define the next chapter of Latino political power in America. Chuck and Mike set the stage for the 2026 battleground: the wide-open California Governor's race, where Latino voters could determine the outcome of a crowded field; the Texas Governor and Senate races; an Arizona Governor's race; a competitive Florida Senate race; and a string of targeted congressional seats along the Texas Rio Grande Valley and in Miami, where a new high-profile candidate just entered the race. Alegre's message to any candidate running in any of these states was consistent: do not assume the Latino vote is coming to you. Go earn it. Go earn it now. He also revealed a striking data point from the Texas election cycle: one in five Latino voters in their survey recalled seeing a Spanish-language political ad. That means roughly 25% of Latino voters were completely unreached by any political message whatsoever. "Twenty-five percent," Alegre said. "That's who you're leaving on the table." The VIX Factor: Reaching the Next Generation For campaigns thinking about digital outreach, Alegre offered a critical distinction. Algorithms on platforms like Facebook or YouTube may flag someone as Hispanic because they watched a Bad Bunny video. That data, he argued, is fundamentally unreliable. TelevisaUnivision's streaming platform VIX -- currently the fastest-growing subscription streaming service in the United States -- operates differently. If someone is on VIX, Alegre said, there is a 99.9% probability they are Hispanic. The platform's targeting, combined with TelevisaUnivision's household data graph that aggregates local TV, national TV, radio, digital, and third-party sources, gives campaigns the most precise Latino targeting available anywhere in the media landscape. "If you want to find a Hispanic voter," Alegre said plainly, "we'll deliver them for you." **His legislative successes include:**

✅ Leading the first Constitutional Carry bill (SB 1212) that ultimately resulted in the successful enactment into law, allowing law-abiding Oklahomans to carry firearms without a permit.

✅ Introducing and supporting Life at Conception legislation and co-sponsoring Oklahoma’s near-total abortion ban that shut down abortion clinics before Roe v. Wade was overturned (HB 4327).

✅ Passing the nation's first Anti-Red Flag Act, preventing firearm confiscation without due process (SB 1081).

✅ Co-sponsoring legislation to declare Oklahoma a Second Amendment Sanctuary State (SB 631).

✅ Introducing bills to assist border states in securing the southern border and combating illegal immigration and human trafficking (SB 1228, SB 1231).

✅ Sponsoring measures to protect private property rights against civil asset forfeiture (SB 621), prohibit warrantless surveillance (SB 38), ban ranked-choice voting (HB 3156), defend parental rights (SB 279), save women's sports by defining sex in law (SB 2), and protect religious freedom (SB 581).

| Hi Peter,

Across our country, farmers are facing a growing challenge.

Fewer people are entering agriculture and conservation careers. Farms are struggling to find the trained workers and technical support they need to protect their land, increase yields, and keep their operations running.

At the same time, farmers are being squeezed by rising costs, uncertainty from Trump’s reckless tariff policies, and years of cuts and instability that have weakened the programs meant to support them. [_**Will you stand with me supporting our farmers by chipping in to the campaign?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127521953/608341174/-1765601992?refcode=BLU_EM_AMDC_2026-03-17_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDkxNzIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTJhNTRjM2QtNDAyMi1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=mLy-qSFX-r18gapPP79FTqGqRC9TUDMxoRs7vAv2EUc=)

Something had to be done. **That is why I introduced two bipartisan bills in Congress last week to strengthen the agricultural conservation workforce.**

My legislation would expand hands-on training programs, support community colleges and apprenticeships, and connect experienced conservation professionals with the next generation through mentorship. These steps will help ensure farmers have the expertise and support they need to protect our land and keep American agriculture strong.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127521955/608341184/-1765601992?refcode=BLU_EM_AMDC_2026-03-17_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDkxNzIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTJhNTRjM2QtNDAyMi1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=mLy-qSFX-r18gapPP79FTqGqRC9TUDMxoRs7vAv2EUc=)
As the daughter of a farmer, **this work is deeply personal to me.** Our farmers are some of the best stewards of our land. But they cannot do it alone, and they cannot succeed if Washington keeps undermining the systems that support them.

That is why this election matters.

We need leaders who will stand up for working farmers, rural communities, and the next generation of conservation professionals. I came to Congress to fight for practical solutions that help everyday people, not billionaires or special interests.

clean_body: Across our country, farmers are facing a growing challenge. | = | Hi Peter, Across our country, farmers are facing a growing challenge. Fewer people are entering agriculture and conservation careers. Farms are struggling to find the trained workers and technical support they need to protect their land, increase yields, and keep their operations running. At the same time, farmers are being squeezed by rising costs, uncertainty from Trump’s reckless tariff policies, and years of cuts and instability that have weakened the programs meant to support them. = | = Something had to be done. That is why I introduced two bipartisan bills in Congress last week to strengthen the agricultural conservation workforce. My legislation would expand hands-on training programs, support community colleges and apprenticeships, and connect experienced conservation professionals with the next generation through mentorship. These steps will help ensure farmers have the expertise and support they need to protect our land and keep American agriculture strong. = As the daughter of a farmer, this work is deeply personal to me. Our farmers are some of the best stewards of our land. But they cannot do it alone, and they cannot succeed if Washington keeps undermining the systems that support them. That is why this election matters. We need leaders who will stand up for working farmers, rural communities, and the next generation of conservation professionals. I came to Congress to fight for practical solutions that help everyday people, not billionaires or special interests. = | | | = | = | = | = | = Thank you for being part of this effort. * Americans who don’t have a passport, who are more likely to come from lower-income families.

* Rural voters who often rely on online and mail-in voter registration.

clean_body: Send an urgent message to Congress right now! | Peter, This is the moment that could decide the 2026 midterms. With his approval ratings dropping further every day, President Trump is upping the pressure on Congress to pass the radical, anti-voter SAVE Act. He knows that the only way for his administration to continue to escape accountability is to rig the midterms and keep his Congressional allies in power. He is even going so far as to say that he will refuse to sign any other bills until Congress passes it. The president thinks that international strife will keep people from noticing what is going on here in the US. | We know that it's hard to keep up with the various anti-voter measures being brought to bear across the country, so here is a refresher on who could be affected by this egregious bill: Married women who have changed their last names and don’t have a birth certificate with their current legal name. Military voters who will no longer be able to use their military ID alone to register. Americans who don’t have a passport, who are more likely to come from lower-income families. Transgender Americans who have changed their legal names. Rural voters who often rely on online and mail-in voter registration. People who have lost documents to natural disasters, and so many more. The stakes have never been clearer. As Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer plainly stated, “The SAVE Act is nothing more than Jim Crow 2.0. It would disenfranchise millions of Americans.” And that is the whole point of this bill. It is not to protect the integrity of our elections from the non-existent voter fraud that the bill’s proponents wring their hands about. It is designed purely to prevent American citizens from voting in new representation in the face of a cratering economy, disastrous foreign policy, and domestic conflicts incited by our own law enforcement. The House of Representatives has already pushed through this terrible legislation. We need to let our senators know we will not sit by as our fundamental right to vote is taken away. The _UNTHINKABLE_ just happened...

Something that has become abundantly clear over the last several days is that adequate force protection measures were not put in place before the initial strikes were launched.
#
Peter, this is Paul Eaton. Major General, U.S. Army, retired.
In the Iraq War, the United States Military was completely unprepared for the war they were asked to fight. Asymmetrical warfare in urban areas against resilient and resourceful adversaries. American Troops went into combat without adequate protection. Thousands were killed and wounded because their vehicles were not up-armored and their body armor was inadequate.
It took a massive outcry — both within the Military and from the public — for corrective action to be taken. VoteVets played a big role in that. But for too many it was too little and too late.
The Trump Administration and Pete Hegseth’s Pentagon chose to start this war, and they own the consequences. Something that has become abundantly clear over the last several days is that adequate force protection measures were not put in place before the initial strikes were launched. Again. American Troops have been killed and seriously wounded because of Hegseth’s failure as Secretary of Defense.
This, from the man who once shared classified battle plans over unsecured channels to people who never should’ve heard them. The right time to fire Pete Hegseth was when those revelations became public last year. He proved he was not up to the job within weeks of his confirmation. The second best time to fire him is now. Our Troops will never be capably led with this abject failure in command.
The unfortunate truth is that Trump surely will not, and Republican leaders in Congress have taken no action to hold him accountable for his failures. That means this job falls to us.
VoteVets will challenge Hegseth relentlessly until he is removed from his position. But the surest way to ensure that happens is by replacing the Republican cowards enabling this war with Democratic majorities in the House and Senate this November.
That work will not come easy, but to defend the young men and women Trump is putting in harm’s way, it is what we must do.

---
Fellow Conservative,

I know how it feels right now. As a guy who's stared down impossible odds overseas, I can sense when fellow patriots get that mix of complacency and doubt creeping in. Minnesota hasn't sent a Republican to the U.S. Senate since 2002. We haven't voted Republican for president since 1976. The polls say it's a long shot, but the Democrats have deep pockets and a messy, well-funded primary between Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan and Rep. Angie Craig. It's easy to think:

_**"Why pour money into this when the deck's stacked?"**_

But Fellow Conservative, that's exactly when the left wins – when good people like you sit on the sidelines, figuring someone else will carry the load. With Tina Smith retiring, this seat is truly open for the first time in a generation. No incumbent shield. A volatile national environment. Friend,

As a doctor, **I see the impacts of policy that falls short every day at work.**

After finishing my medical training, I wanted to be a part of the solution to improve access to healthcare in rural areas.

As a family doctor, I see people of every age, of every profession, of every race, and every socioeconomic class. I take care of people who have lifelong chronic illnesses, who struggle with mental health, and who are grappling with affording healthcare.

And serving as the Chief Medical Officer for the Central Valley, I’ve been deployed during fires to take care of firefighters. When I’m deployed, I’m the only doctor with a team of EMTs and a couple of nurses.

[My experiences have shaped my views on policy on issues including accessible and affordable healthcare and emergency preparedness, and it’s why I’m running for Congress. body:
I need your help to keep Michigan blue

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. [To unsubscribe from this email list, please click here.](https://act.haleyformi.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?&t=1&akid=2466%2E49239%2Eps5cJn)

---
**The chair of the NRSC said on national TV: "We are going to win in Michigan."**
**[null, if you’re ready to prove MAGA Republicans wrong, will you chip in $5 right now to help us keep Michigan blue?](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/15557?t=3&akid=2466%2E49239%2Eps5cJn)**
That comment wasn’t casual. It was a signal.

Here’s why: GOP megadonors, including a Texas oil billionaire backing Mike Rogers, have already poured millions into this race. But polling still shows us in a statistical tie.
So GOP operatives are putting out the Bat Signal that Michigan is their top priority.

They’re rallying donors and preparing to flood this state with even more megadonor money.
